item.title: 'You have no right to comment on my private life' - Kevin De Bruyne hits back at Napoli exit rumours amid PSV Eindhoven transfer links
item.description: SSC Napoli v Torino FC - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Kevin De Bruyne has hit out at the Italian media for creating a hostile environment for his family amid ongoing speculation regarding his future at Napoli. The Belgian playmaker spoke out ahead of a highly anticipated return to the Etihad Stadium for a Champions League encounter with his former club, Manchester City. Frustration over privacy and transfer links De Bruyne has expressed his deep frustration with recent reports suggesting he could leave the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in the January transfer window . The veteran playmaker, who has been linked with a move to PSV Eindhoven, used his pre-match press conference to address a recent interview given by his wife in Belgium that he feels was intentionally misinterpreted by the Italian press to fuel exit rumours. "I’m quite sorry about it all to be honest. If you go and read the article, which you have not read, you will understand what she said. I was away in Belgium and then a lot of things were being said and there were a lot of negative reactions towards my wife," De Bruyne said, as quoted by Football Italia . He voiced specific anger over the publication of photos of his private residence, adding, "I saw photos of my house in the press, which is not good. I know that journalists in Italy have created this situation and I don’t know why. You do not know my private life, you have no right to comment on my private life. It was an unpleasant situation for me and my wife." The veteran playmaker tight-lipped on Napoli future De Bruyne has remained tight-lipped over his long-term future with Napoli, admitting that his approaching 36th birthday leaves him with plenty to weigh up amid his ongoing contract situation . Despite the uncertainty surrounding his next move, the veteran midfielder insisted his focus remains firmly on giving everything for the Partenopei. Rather than getting drawn into speculation, the Belgian playmaker stressed that his immediate priority is maintaining his strong form and helping the club navigate a demanding campaign. "I can’t say very much at this point. I’ve played at 400% so far. I’m not 20 years old anymore, I’m almost 36, so there are lots of things to consider. Right now, there’s not a lot to say. I’m playing well, I’m trying to help the team to do well. There have been lots of challenges this year and a lot of things have happened," he explained. Tactical evolution and return to Manchester Despite the off-field distractions, De Bruyne insisted he is satisfied with his individual performances for Massimiliano Allegri's side this season. He noted that his role on the pitch continues to evolve as he adapts to different systems and spaces within the game. The Belgian emphasised that his ability to read the pitch remains his greatest strength, regardless of where he is positioned by the coaching staff. item.title: Tyson Fury reveals schizophrenia, bipolar disorder
item.description: Former world heavyweight boxing champion, Tyson Fury, has disclosed that he was diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder in a forthcoming Netflix documentary about his life and career. According to Deadline , Fury made the revelation in the feature-length documentary titled Tyson Fury , which is scheduled for release later this month. The boxer said he was diagnosed with schizophrenia shortly after defeating Wladimir Klitschko in 2015 to become the world heavyweight champion. He also disclosed that he received a bipolar disorder diagnosis in 2017. Reflecting on his mental health struggles in the documentary, Fury described experiencing periods of severe psychological distress. “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in. I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100% thought at times I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much,” he reportedly said. Fury also recounted experiencing intense anxiety that frequently woke him in the middle of the night. He said he eventually sought professional help from a psychiatrist in London, who assessed him through a series of questions and identified depression, anxiety and bipolar disorder. The documentary also features contributions from his wife, Paris Fury, and father, John Fury, who discuss his mental health challenges. The post Tyson Fury reveals schizophrenia, bipolar disorder appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Dortmund and Chelsea target Williams-Barnett set for Tottenham contract extension
item.description: Dortmund and Chelsea target Williams-Barnett set for Tottenham contract extension Borussia Dortmund appear to have lost out in the race for Luca Williams-Barnett, according to a report in the Telegraph. The 18-year-old is believed to be on the verge of agreeing a long-term contract extension with his current employers Tottenham Hotspur. Fellow Premier League outfit Chelsea alongside the Westphalians are believed to have recently made inquiries for the midfielder. Other high-profile clubs such as Bayern Munich, Manchester City and Manchester United have also been linked with him. The England U-19 international has made his first three Premier League appearances for Spurs in recent weeks, scoring once.

item.title: Stats: Here’s how Barcelona have fared without Lamine Yamal in the squad
item.description: Stats: Here’s how Barcelona have fared without Lamine Yamal in the squad Hansi Flick will face his first Barcelona match without Lamine Yamal this season when the Catalans travel to Azerbaijan to meet Sabah in the Champions League on Wednesday, November 25. The 19-year-old winger has been ruled out because of mild discomfort in his right ankle, with the club confirming that his absence is a precautionary measure and that he is expected to return against Deportivo on Sunday. Yamal’s absence ends an uninterrupted run of 17 appearances in Barcelona’s official matches this season, having accumulated 1,445 minutes, scoring 13 goals and providing 13 assists. However, the German manager has previous experience managing without his most influential young forward, and Barcelona’s results suggest the squad has gradually become better equipped to cope with his absence. Barcelona’s record without Lamine Yamal under Hansi Flick Since Flick took charge, Barcelona have played 17 matches without Yamal, recording 11 victories, five defeats and one draw. During the 2024/25 campaign, Barcelona struggled to maintain consistency without their right winger. They won just two of five matches, beating Brest 3-0 in the Champions League and Barbastro 4-0 in the Copa del Rey. The remaining three fixtures exposed their difficulties, as defeats against Real Sociedad and Atletico Madrid, alongside a draw against Celta Vigo, left Flick with limited reasons for optimism when his teenage forward was unavailable. Barcelona improved considerably during the 2025/26 season The picture changed significantly in 2025/26 when Barcelona collected nine victories from the 12 matches Yamal missed. Notably, their ability to produce positive results without him was particularly evident before his season-ending injury in April. Flick’s side defeated Newcastle United, Valencia, Getafe, Real Oviedo and Slavia Prague during earlier spells without the winger. Sevilla provided a notable exception, handing Barcelona a 1-4 defeat. Yamal’s subsequent hamstring injury forced him to miss the final six league fixtures. Barcelona won four of those matches, overcoming Getafe 2-0, Osasuna 2-1, Real Madrid 2-0 and Real Betis 3-1. Barcelona will be without Lamine Yamal against Sabah. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) They also suffered defeats against Alaves and Valencia. Real Madrid victory showed Barcelona can cope without Yamal Perhaps the strongest evidence of Barcelona’s ability to function without Yamal came against Real Madrid. Flick’s team secured a 2-0 victory at Spotify Camp Nou, a result that confirmed their La Liga title triumph and showed that collective performance could compensate for the absence of an individual attacking difference-maker. That precedent offers encouragement ahead of the trip to Azerbaijan, although the circumstances are different. item.title: Real Madrid president was ‘obsessed’ with French winger in the summer; will return on one condition – Romano
item.description: Real Madrid president was ‘obsessed’ with French winger in the summer; will return on one condition – Romano Real Madrid’s pursuit of Michael Olise last summer was no secret, and every move the club made towards the player was public knowledge throughout the saga. Eventually, however, the deal did not move ahead as Bayern Munich refused to sell Olise despite the player deeply longing for a move to Real Madrid. Eventually, Los Blancos brought in Yan Diomande for a record transfer fee and the player has settled into Jose Mourinho’s dynamics well. Yet, there have been talks of Olise still being a potential target Florentino Perez is attached to. The latest information As reported by the ever-reliable Fabrizio Romano (h/t Madrid Xtra ) now, Olise was a massive obsession for Perez last summer, and that was the foundation for all of Real Madrid’s persistent efforts. Perez was obsessed with Olise. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) To date, everyone at Real Madrid is said to be ‘in love’ with Olise and what he brings to the field, especially Perez. As for the player’s future, Bayern Munich are set to offer Olise a new contract renewal soon and it remains to be seen what the player decides. At this point, his decision will steer Real Madrid’s interest. Los Blancos continue to be deeply interested in signing him, but will only take a step forward and negotiate with Olise if Bayern Munich inform them that he is for sale. They will preserve relations with the German club as their priority. An atrocious price tag Olise will be offered a renewal. (Photo by Mattia Ozbot/Getty Images) As relayed earlier this month, the Bavarians have now set their asking fee for a potential Olise departure, and the sum will send the eyes of most clubs across the world rolling. The German champions, after all, are said to have placed a €300 million price tag on the Frenchman, and see that to be fair compensation for his services. Needless to say, however, that sum is simply unheard of and not feasible even for Real Madrid. Real Madrid, in that sense, were said to have taken a step back in the race after hearing the price. If Olise can push Bayern and have them admit he is for sale, however, the power dynamics of the saga will shift significantly and give Real Madrid more skin in the game.

item.title: Commanders’ Antonio Williams reveals bold call that led to game-winning field goal vs. Bengals
item.description: Amber Searls-Imagn Images Commanders’ Antonio Williams reveals bold call that led to game-winning field goal vs. Bengals appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Washington Commanders trusted Antonio Williams twice in the biggest moments of Monday night . Fortunately, the wide receiver delivered both times to help secure a dramatic 22-20 victory over the Cincinnati Bengals. Trailing 20-19 with just 46 seconds remaining, Washington needed a quick spark to get into field-goal range. Head coach Dan Quinn dialed up a familiar concept. Jayden Daniels found Williams for a 22-yard gain before going right back to the same play moments later. Williams responded with another explosive reception. This time, he gained 41 yards to put the Commanders in position for Drew Stevens’ game-winning 26-yard field goal . After the game, Williams revealed that Washington ran the exact same play on both decisive snaps. He emphasized the confidence Quinn and Daniels had in him to make something happen under pressure. Antonio Williams on his final two receptions: Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "The same play back-to-back. Coach trusts me to make those and in those moments. You dream of those on Monday Night Football." pic.twitter.com/55NpKlrx0g https://t.co/742GFkxGX7 — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) November 24, 2026 “The same play back-to-back,” Williams said regarding his final two catches. “Coach trusts me to make those and in those moments. You dream of those on Monday Night Football.” Williams finished with a career-high nine receptions for 122 yards on 11 targets. He became a major difference-maker in a Washington passing attack adjusting to Terry McLaurin’s season-ending injury. His late-game heroics also highlighted the growing connection between him and Daniels. This is particularly true as the Commanders look for dependable playmakers during the stretch run. Washington improved to 4-5-1 with its second consecutive victory. This gave the team renewed momentum in the NFC playoff race. Williams had steadily earned a larger role throughout the season. He entered Monday with 28 catches for 326 yards and two touchdowns. His performance against Cincinnati, though, could represent a turning point in his campaign. When the game demanded two big plays, Washington went back to Williams. More importantly, he delivered. Ja’Marr Chase had five catches for 31 yards on nine targets. Like, for real. Tee Higgins had two catches for 43 yards on three targets. That’s the equivalent of a skunk. Daronte Jones, we got you. For real. The blitz scheme worked. Grade: A-plus Special Teams Drew Stevens, y’all Grade: A-plus Coaching I’ve been so critical of coaching in this space. And for real reasons. But this was something different. Gotta give credit where it’s deserved. And, it must be said: Daronte Jones is reaching another level. Grade: A-plus

item.title: Jensen Huang’s return has calmed markets but fears of an AI bubble still run deep
item.description: Nvidia's decision to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO pushed the AI computing company's stocks up more than 30 percent Monday. But the model of circular financing increasingly underwriting the AI boom still has some analysts worried that the party can't last forever.

item.title: Agit Kabayel is the ringmaster of a new heavyweight circus
item.description: There was a time when an American was in one corner of every single heavyweight world-title fight. Every fight from the end of the bare-knuckle period to the end of the 1980s. The fall of the Wall and the arrival of the Eastern Bloc boxers changed the landscape forever, but still Americans held the grip on a title that seemed forever destined to be owned by a man from Philadelphia or Houston or Louisville. That is all over now, possibly gone for good. Deontay Wilder was the last American heavyweight world champion, and he was beaten in seven rounds by Tyson Fury in early 2020; he challenged Fury the following year, lost again, and that was the last time an American came anywhere near the world heavyweight title. Agit Kabayel after stopping Zhilei Zhang in early 2025 (Getty) Close to 30 years ago, Don King announced that he was searching for the next American heavyweight superstar; that desperate search is continuing today, and at the same time gyms in Tirana, Moscow and Lagos are full of heavyweight dreamers. This Saturday, in front of 50,000 fans in Dusseldorf , Germany’s Agit Kabayel defends his WBC heavyweight title when he meets the unbeaten Nelson Hysa of Albania. It is a bizarrely cosmopolitan clash. Kabayel, on his way directly to the WBC title, stopped in succession a Russian, a Chinese fighter, a Croatian, a Pole, and a Cuban. There is not an American heavyweight left to come even close to pushing Kabayel. The top American is arguably a man called Michael Hunter, who is 38 and had his best win in 2018. Hunter is the only American worth a top-20 ranking, and he is lost in a turbulent sea of boxers from a dozen countries. A Nigerian, an Australian and about seven British boxers are in front of Hunter. Where is Rocky Balboa when you need him? Right now, Kabayel might just be the best of the four heavyweight champions, with Daniel Dubois , Filip Hrgovic and Murat Gassiev holding the other belts in the wake of Oleksandr Usyk giving up all of the gold . Kabayel vs Hysa Tale of the tape Kabayel – Record: 27-0 (19 KOs); height: 6ft 3in; reach: 80in; age: 34. Hysa – Record: 25-0 (23 KOs); height: 6ft 5in; reach: 79in; age: 42. And Kabayel, 34, can look good against Hysa who, at 42, is wandering close to George Foreman’s ancient territory. It will be fun until Kabayel does his thing and breaks Hysa’s heart after about six rounds of body shots. Kabayel started three of his last four bouts as the underdog, fighting men with unbeaten records or a genuine claim to a higher ranking. On each occasion, he slowly prodded away and calmly broke the spirit and desire of a trio of quality men. A similar win against Hysa, who is a big lump and offers a lot of bulk for Kabayel to target, will raise Kabayel’s profile against the other champions. Nelson Hysa (top) last fought in August, stopping Thomas Narmo in two rounds (Getty) It will also leave Kabayel and his devoted following in a very strong position next year, when we know what Anthony Joshua and Fury are

item.title: The Davis Cup is broken but Carlos Alcaraz can save it
item.description: For nearly five months of this year, Carlos Alcaraz was sidelined, nursing a wrist injury which threatened to derail his entire season. Just three months on from his return, and despite managing two different injury concerns, the Spaniard has rewritten the history books and could yet send another record tumbling before signing off for Christmas. Four days after claiming his first ATP Finals title, becoming the youngest man – at just 23 – to complete the clean sweep of all four majors and the season-ending individual crown, he could join only Andre Agassi , Novak Djokovic , and Roger Federer in the pantheon of greats to also win the Davis Cup . The tennis calendar doesn’t so much slow to a halt over Christmas as barrel almost cleanly through into the next season, with a rapid turnaround for those heading from the ATP Finals in Turin to the Davis Cup in Bologna this week. But despite Alcaraz’s frenetic autumn schedule, winning three back-to-back tournaments in Vienna, Paris, and Turin, and the wear and tear on his body, he is in spellbinding form and highly fancied to lead Spain to a first title since 2019. The Davis Cup has struggled for relevance in recent years. The fact that it takes place annually lowers the stakes and drama of what claims to be the ‘World Cup’ of tennis, while the torturously convoluted system of play-offs and qualifying ties makes it difficult for the casual fan to understand. Add to that top players’ reluctance to risk injury, and their prioritising of the ATP Tour in an utterly relentless calendar, means the big names tend to drop out and viewers’ interest follows the same downward curve. So it is a huge boost to the tournament that although home star Jannik Sinner remains a long-term absentee, Alcaraz, who missed last year’s Finals, is back, while the Italians – led again by Flavio Cobolli – are fielding a raft of top names including Matteo Berrettini and Lorenzo Musetti . In total, nine top-10 players across both singles and doubles will take part, and seven of the singles top-20. Three-time defending champions Italy face underdogs South Korea before taking on either Felix Auger-Aliassime ’s Canada or Czechia, spearheaded by the top-20 pairing of Jakub Mensik and Jiri Lehecka. The bottom half sees Germany and Spain take on Great Britain and Austria respectively. GB are playing their last tie under the leadership of Leon Smith , who will end a near-17 year stint as captain after this week . There are no faces left from the Finals-winning squad of 2015, the zenith of Smith’s tenure, but there is an exciting mix of the old and new: this year’s breakout British star, Wimbledon semi-finalist Arthur Fery , alongside stalwart Cameron Norrie . Most significantly, GB possess a lethal doubles partnership in world No 1 Henry Patten and No 3 Neal Skupski , who between them have won three of the last four Grand Slams. item.title: 49ers win in Mexico and Bills stay top - NFL week 11
item.description: The San Francisco 49ers and Buffalo Bills remain the pacesetters in each conference of the NFL after both won again. The 49ers beat the Minnesota Vikings in the last of a record nine international games this season to take their record to 9-1. They lead the way in the NFC, with the Chicago Bears and their divisional rivals the Detroit Lions next best on 8-2. Buffalo improved to 9-1 for the first time since 1991 and lead the AFC from another pair of divisional rivals, with the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos on 8-2. The Cincinnati Bengals are 7-3 after being undone by a walk-off field goal for the Washington Commanders. 49ers outsmart Vikings defence Mexico hosted the first regular-season game to be played outside the US in October 2005, and the NFL returned to the country on Sunday following a four-year absence. After being redeveloped for the 2026 World Cup, the Azteca Stadium staged its sixth NFL game and the third involving San Francisco, who kicked off this season's international series by beating the Los Angeles Rams in Australia in week one. Sunday's game pitted the league's best offence against the best defence and was the first international game to be played in the primetime slot. The Vikings defence had not conceded more than 23 points in a game this season, but the 49ers offence outsmarted them in front of 85,612 fans in Mexico City. The 49ers scored four touchdowns in the first half - two by George Kittle - before running out 35-10 winners. Mike Evans returned after missing three games with an Achilles problem to finish with 109 receiving yards and a touchdown. With the game played at high altitude - about 7,220ft (2,240m) above sea level - some players used oxygen masks on the sidelines. San Francisco face another test of their Super Bowl credentials next Sunday at home to the defending champions, the 6-4 Seattle Seahawks, who were one of six teams on their bye this week. San Francisco linebacker Fred Warner has Mexican heritage and his first name is Federico [Getty Images] Giants secure statement win The Jacksonville Jaguars entered week 11 with the best regular-season record over the past 12 months - they had lost only twice - and had scored more than 30 points in each of their past four games. Yet the New York Giants managed to stifle the Jaguars for three quarters and led 20-6 heading into what proved to be a dramatic final quarter. The Jaguars had to settle for a field goal after a controversial call denied them a touchdown, but they still threatened a fightback as they cut the deficit to five. The Giants offence did enough to stop the Jags getting one more possession, though, and secure a 23-18 home win. It was the first time the NFC East leaders have beaten a team with a winning record this season and they are now 6-3-1, while the 7-3 Jags remain in charge of the AFC South. item.title: Nigerians Firmly Behind APC Despite Criticism And Insults — Yari
item.description: The Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’azeez Yari Abubakar, has said the massive turnout at the party’s governorship campaign flag-off in Zamfara State demonstrates the people’s acceptance of the party despite what he described as campaigns of calumny and insults against it. Yari said the APC was consolidating its support base to secure victory at all levels in the 2027 general elections, attributing the party’s growing acceptance to its closeness to the masses. He stated this on Monday during the APC campaign flag-off held in Talata-Mafara, which attracted party faithful, support groups and members of the public. All Progressives Congress governorship campaign flag-off in Zamfara State on Monday, November 23, 2026. Crowds of party supporters welcomed Governor Dauda Lawal’s motorcade to Talata-Mafara town before proceeding to the town’s Eid ground, venue of the rally. Speaking at the event, Senator Yari said the large turnout reflected the enthusiasm and commitment of party members and supporters towards the party’s preparations for the 2027 elections. “Make sure this message gets to the public: we are determined to deliver victory for the APC, from President Tinubu down to members of the State House of Assembly. “The overwhelming response to our call demonstrates that, despite the insults and campaigns against the APC, the people of Zamfara have understood our message and are firmly behind the party,” he said. The Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’azeez Yari Abubakar, and Governor Radda Dikko during the party’s governorship campaign flag-off in Zamfara State, on Monday, November 23, 2026. Also speaking, Governor Dauda Lawal expressed gratitude to party supporters for their show of solidarity, while commending the people for their resilience and commitment to peaceful coexistence. He reaffirmed his administration’s resolve to promote inclusive governance, equitable development and sustained engagement with communities across the state. “This crowd speaks for itself; there is very little to say other than to thank Almighty God. Whenever I turn around and see this mammoth crowd of supporters, I am filled with gratitude. “At this point, I will simply say, let us wait for election day and, ultimately, the swearing-in day,” Lawal said. The APC campaign train is expected to move to other local government areas of Zamfara State as the party intensifies its mobilisation and grassroots engagement ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Waste crisis: LAWMA launches nighttime evacuation gangs
item.description: …Plans over 10 regional offices ahead of Yuletide By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA) has launched a nighttime waste evacuation operation across the state to tackle mounting refuse heaps and restore environmental sanitation ahead of the Christmas and New Year festivities. The exercise, which commenced on Monday night, began along the Isheri–Igando–LASU–Iba corridor, with sanitation teams and heavy-duty equipment deployed to clear identified waste black spots. LAWMA’s Acting Managing Director, Olajuwon Akinyemi, led the operation at Igando Bus Stop alongside the Acting Executive Director of Operations, Olorunwa Tijani, and the Executive Director of Finance, Kunle Adebiyi. Speaking during the exercise, Akinyemi said the nighttime evacuation would be extended to other major entry routes and high-traffic corridors, including Ojota–Ikorodu Road, Mushin–Moshalashi axis and Lekki–Ajah corridor. He said the operation was aimed at restoring Lagos’s environmental appeal and providing a cleaner and healthier atmosphere for residents and visitors expected in the state during the busy December holiday season. To prevent cleared locations from becoming refuse dumps again, the agency said it was partnering with traditional institutions across the state to strengthen community monitoring and enforcement. Beyond the immediate clean-up exercise, Akinyemi announced plans to establish more than 10 regional offices across Lagos as part of efforts to decentralise the authority’s operations. He described the restructuring as non-negotiable, saying the regional offices would improve operational coordination, bring waste management services closer to communities, strengthen accountability and ensure faster responses to sanitation challenges. The LAWMA boss appealed to residents to remain patient with the state government as it works to address waste management challenges across the metropolis. He also urged residents to promptly report service failures by Private Sector Participation (PSP) waste operators through the authority’s official communication channels to enable it to enforce compliance. item.title: JJ Redick Credits Lakers’ Early-Season Success To One Special Factor
item.description: Nov 23, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick in the second half against the Utah Jazz at Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images The Utah Jazz are among the few teams the Los Angeles Lakers have lost to this season. Although they lost to Utah on Wednesday , the Purple and Gold redeemed themselves on Monday night, posting a 109-94 victory to improve to 15-3 for the season. Monday night’s win was a product of several factors, one of which was Luka Doncic ‘s sustained offensive brilliance . With 28 points, four rebounds, eight assists, and a steal, the Lakers’ superstar led the winning effort. Even so, one could argue that this win belonged to the role players. The grit and hustle shown by players like Jake LaRavia , Matisse Thybulle , Ziaire Williams , and Collin Sexton at key moments defined the Lakers’ performance. During his postgame press conference , head coach JJ Redick had to acknowledge this. While speaking about what makes this team special, Redick stated: “I think they’re all really grateful to be here, the Lakers. They’re all really grateful to be on this team and be a part of the group. I know Matisse has expressed that to me on a couple of occasions.” “You know, for Z, Matisse, and Q, they’ve experienced adversity in their careers in different ways. I think that gratitude piece is like, they’re all in a situation- Jake, we’ve been around him enough to know. But they’re all in a situation where they put the team first, and they’re putting their egos aside.” “That stuff matters,” Redick continued. “It’s one of the reasons our group has had early success because we said on day one, we wanted this season to be about the team and not any one individual, and so far, it’s been that.” As Redick mentioned, much of the Lakers’ approach this year has been guided by the shared common goal. From the roster-building approach to the team-building activities led by Luka Doncic in the summer, the Purple and Gold have prioritized the whole rather than the individual. To that end, the results early in the campaign have been promising. While L.A. is clearly Doncic’s team, with the superstar logging unreal performances on a nightly basis, the contributions of the role players have been beyond critical. Whether this involves Sexton’s hustle, Thybulle’s disruptive work , Grimes’ scoring outbursts , or Williams’ two-way contributions, the Lakers have benefited greatly from the unit’s willingness to make sacrifices for the team. In many ways, Monday night’s victory captured this sentiment perfectly. As mentioned earlier, even though Doncic led the charge, it was the role players who really stood out. Jake LaRavia was nothing short of spectacular on both ends of the floor. While his 15 points on 6-10 shooting deserve attention, the Purple and Gold would not be in a position to win the game if LaRavia hadn’t crashed the boards the way he did. item.title: Arizona men’s basketball downs Colorado State in Maui Invitational opener
item.description: LAHAINIA, HI- NOVEMBER 23: JJ Mandaquit #23 of the Arizona Wildcats drives to the basket against Justin Menard #3 of the Colorado State Rams in the second half during a first round Southwest Maui Invitational college basketball game at the Lahaina Civic Center on November 23, 2026 in Lahaina, Hawaii. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) | Getty Images With three games in three days, Tommy Lloyd had a goal of giving his bench more playing time to ease the burden off his starting five. Lloyd did play the reserves more than in the previous two outings, but a pesky Colorado State team kept him from subbing as much as he’d have liked. No. 8 Arizona beat the Rams 96-83 on Monday night in its opening game of the Maui Invitational. The Wildcats (5-1) will face Providence, which beat VCU in overtime earlier in the tourney, at 3 p.m. MT Tuesday in the semifinals. All five starters scored in double figures for the UA, with Ivan Kharchenkov having another all-around masterful performance with 24 points, six rebounds, six assists and four steals. Caleb Holt went for 20 with nine rebounds and four assists, while Motiejus Krivas had 17 with seven rebounds and five assists, JJ Mandaquit scored a career-high 15 and Derek Dixon chipped in 10. Mandaquit, a Hawai’i native playing in front of roughly 50 friends and family, was 5 of 7 from the field and 4 of 6 from 3. He’s 11 of 22 from outside this season. Arizona shot 54.7 percent overall and made 12 of 27 3s, getting multiple triples from four players for the first time since the 2024 NCAA Tournament opener against Akron. That included ones from Maksim Brnovic and Bryce James . The bench scored 10 points, double what it produced against Auburn and UConn, but the five reserves used still only played 38 minutes. Colorado State (4-2) shot 45.8 percent, including 51.9 percent in the 2 nd half, and was 12 of 33 from 3. The Rams outrebounded the UA 32-30 and limited the Wildcats to six offensive boards. The UA led 50-34 at halftime, its second 50-point half of the season and most in the 1 st half of a Maui Invitational game since dropping 51 on Chaminade in 2000. Threes by Holt and Mandaquit got Arizona up 23 but then Colorado State scored nine in a row. The Rams’ 2-3 zone got the Wildcats out of sorts for a bit, leading to a nearly 3-minute stretch without scoring before Krivas tipped in a Holt miss in traffic. Not long after that Krivas picked up his third foul, heading to the bench with just over 14 minutes left. A 3-point play by Mandaquit got the UA back up 65-49 with 11:55 to go. It was his first made 2-pointer of the season. Colorado State’s 3-point shooting got it back in the game, hitting four straight perimeter shots and 5 of 6 overall to get within 72-65. Lloyd called timeout with 7:58 remaining, and the play he called during the break resulted in Holt scoring inside against the zone. item.title: Omo Agege attack: ‘Enough is enough’, arrest, prosecute perpetrators – Keyamo tells police
item.description: The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has condemned the killing of four persons in Ughelli, Delta State, following an outbreak of political violence, calling on security agencies to arrest and prosecute those responsible. Keyamo, in a statement issued on Monday, described the incident in his hometown as disturbing and said several other persons sustained injuries and were receiving treatment. He expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and wished those injured a speedy recovery. The minister also condemned the killing of a tricycle operator allegedly by supporters of a political party in Asaba on November 7, 2026, urging law enforcement agencies to investigate both incidents and bring the perpetrators to justice. “I have been in touch with the top hierarchy of law enforcement agencies in the last one month over the rising wave of political violence and violent rhetoric in Delta State,” he said. Keyamo lamented that Delta, which had enjoyed relative political peace since 1999, was witnessing a disturbing rise in violence, insisting that political disagreements should not degenerate into killings. “Since 1999, Delta State has been a relatively peaceful state, politically. Our disagreements have never led to violence and killings. We are all brothers and sisters who went to the same primary, secondary and tertiary institutions, and we all know ourselves and our families so well. There is ABSOLUTELY NO NEED for a descent into violence,” he said. He also criticised the slogan, “Rig and Die”, allegedly promoted by some political actors in Delta State and elsewhere, describing it as capable of escalating political tension and encouraging violence. The minister urged those promoting the slogan to reconsider their position, publicly withdraw it and apologise for overheating the political atmosphere. “Those who have promoted the mantra of ‘Rig and Die’ in Delta State and elsewhere should have a rethink, publicly withdraw it, and apologise for overheating the political temperature in the State and country. As can be seen, anyone can be a victim,” he said. Keyamo maintained that only law enforcement agencies had the authority to deal with offenders, warning political leaders against encouraging their supporters to attack other citizens. He described such conduct as a sign of desperation and called on the Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, to urgently address residents and warn those threatening violence. “I call on our leader and my elder brother, the Governor of Delta State and the Chief Security Officer of the State, Rt. Hon. Elder Sheriff Oborevwori, to urgently address Deltans and read the Riot Act against those who are threatening fire and brimstone. “Enough is enough,” he said. item.title: Can the Commanders make a run after beating the Bengals? Jayden Daniels makes the case
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Can the Commanders make a run after beating the Bengals? Jayden Daniels makes the case appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Nobody on ESPN’s ‘Monday Night Countdown’ crew gave the Washington Commanders much of a shot against Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals . After pulling off a wild 22-20 upset at Northwest Stadium, quarterback Jayden Daniels laughed off the pregame picks with Scott Van Pelt on SportsCenter and delivered a bold message about where Washington goes from here. “I think it could lead to a run,” Daniels said. "I think it could lead to a run." 👀 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Commanders QB Jayden Daniels sits with @notthefakeSVP following their upset win over the Bengals 🏈 pic.twitter.com/NuGvO55YFu — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) November 24, 2026 Looking at how the Commanders clawed out Monday night’s win, he has a real argument. Washington sputtered early in the pouring rain, prompting a heated sideline outburst from wide receiver Stefon Diggs as the offense stalled. Instead of folding, Daniels flipped the switch and orchestrated six consecutive scoring drives. He finished with 344 total yards, completing 23 of 35 passes for 289 yards while adding 55 rushing yards on six carries without committing a turnover. His best work came when the margin for error disappeared. Trailing 20-19 with 46 seconds left and no timeouts, Daniels marched Washington 64 yards down the field. He connected with rookie wideout Antonio Williams, who racked up nine catches for 122 yards, on back-to-back strikes of 22 and 42 yards. Rookie kicker Drew Stevens then nailed a 26-yard field goal as time expired to finish 5-for-5 on the night, spoiling a 300-yard, two-touchdown outing from Burrow. That resilience has completely changed the vibe in Washington . Now sitting at 4-5-1, the Commanders own consecutive prime-time wins after upsetting the New York Giants in Week 10. They still trail New York (6-3-1) and the Dallas Cowboys (5-6) in the NFC East, though Washington holds the head-to-head tiebreaker over the first-place Giants. With favorable road matchups against the Arizona Cardinals and Tennessee Titans up next, Daniels and the Commanders have every reason to believe their postseason push is officially underway. item.title: Ex-Baltimore Orioles Starter Trevor Rogers Signs with Chicago Cubs for $120 Million
item.description: PotentiaL New York Mets free agent: Baltimore Orioles LHP Trevor Rogers pitches against the Milwaukee Brewers on September 19. Getty BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 19: Trevor Rogers #28 of the Baltimore Orioles pitches in the sixth inning against the Milwaukee Brewers at Oriole Park at Camden Yards on September 19, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Greg Fiume/Getty Images) Getty Ex-Baltimore Orioles starter Trevor Rogers is headed to the North Side of Chicago on a five-year deal. Per multiple reports, the Chicago Cubs and Rogers have agreed to terms on a new contract. MLB Network’s Jon Morosi was first to the agreement, and Ken Rosenthal noted that it’s a five-year pact between the Cubs and Rogers. The deal is pending a physical, but undoubtedly a big splash for the Chicago Cubs, and an equally big loss for the Orioles. Trevor Rogers, 29, joined the Baltimore Orioles following a 2024 trade with the Miami Marlins. Update: It’s a $120 million guaranteed deal for Rogers. $24 million AAV for the 29-year-old. More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Reportedly Interested in Bringing Back Former 3-Year Player Looking at Trevor Rogers Tenure with the Orioles Getty BALTIMORE, MARYLAND – SEPTEMBER 19: Trevor Rogers #28 of the Baltimore Orioles pitches in the sixth inning against the Milwaukee Brewers at Oriole Park at Camden Yards on September 19, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Greg Fiume/Getty Images) Across parts of three seasons with the Orioles, Trevor Rogers made 52 starts. Over those 52 starts, Rogers posted an ERA of 3.41 with 272 strikeouts in 298+ innings. 2025 was undoubtedly the best campaign of his career, as the southpaw Rogers boasted an ERA of 1.81 over 18 starts. His All-Star campaign in 2021 was also impressive, but Rogers posted a pWAR of 5.3 in 2025, which is a dominant mark considering he only made 18 starts. In 2026, Rogers took a bit of a step back, as he struggled in parts of the season. Across 30 starts this past season, Rogers held an ERA of 4.03 with 157 strikeouts in 169.2 innings. Still a pretty quality campaign, and his 30 starts proved he can be a very durable starter, which is likely what led to this new five-year deal. item.title: Patriots HC Mike Vrabel Calls Out and Challenges Team Amid Skid
item.description: New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel called out and challenged his team amid its skid to .500, losing Drake Maye. Getty Everything that could possibly go wrong for Mike Vrabel and the New England Patriots has gone wrong in 2026. From off-field scandals to injuries to underperformance, the Patriots find themselves at .500 going into Thanksgiving, and arguably lucky to be there. The Patriots are now losers of two in a row and three of their last four games. Worse, starting quarterback Drake Maye joined the long list of injured players, and it now looks like he’s going to be done for the season. That gave Vrabel and the Patriots a bye week to regroup before getting back on the field and trying to find a way to compete with Tommy DeVito as their starting quarterback. New England Patriots HC Mike Vrabel Challenged His Team Drake Maye left the Patriots’ game in Germany at the end of the first drive. It seemingly sucked the life from the team, and nobody was able to play well in any facet of the game. If the Patriots want to make a push for the playoffs, they’ll need to be better as a group. Mike Vrabel knows that well. “Well, just play better,” Mike Vrabel said . “Again, I think that we have a lot of confidence in Tommy [DeVito]. I think just doing the little things better, not hurting ourselves, negative plays, making sure that we stay balanced.” The Patriots have given up 80 points over their last two games. That’s on the defense, regardless of whether or not Maye is healthy. Special teams haven’t been special, and turnovers have been an issue for the offense all season long. None of it is good enough. “Offensively, taking care of the football,” Vrabel said. “Defensively, limiting the X plays and finding ways to create turnovers. I think that we’ve been close on special teams. We get one opportunity, usually, the way that it plays out with a punt return and trying to get Marcus [Jones] going there. That was such a weapon for us and has been a weapon in the past. Then making sure that on the ability to cover kickoffs, not having the one that gets out to the 45.” The reality is that Maye isn’t replaceable for the Patriots. It doesn’t matter who they play. So, Vrabel needs his entire team to step up and make up the difference. “Those are the things that we have to continue to do no matter who’s playing quarterback. Those are things that are going to be important. Protecting inside out, not letting pressure into the middle of the pocket that disrupts the timing of the play. All the same things no matter who the quarterback is,” Vrabel said. Vrabel on His Frustrations with How Patriots Play The biggest concern for the Patriots is that most of these issues aren’t new. They’ve dealt with turnover concerns all season long. They’ve had a defense that isn’t playing to its potential. item.title: 5 Takeaways After Lakers Hold Off A Furious Jazz Comeback In 109-94 Victory
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers avoided a furious comeback loss, holding off a Utah Jazz comeback to secure a 109-94 victory. Although the final score suggests a comfortable night, the game was far more competitive. Utah actually outscored Los Angeles in the paint and finished with a slight rebounding advantage. Still, the Lakers made the difference with transition offense and some smart play from their MVP. Luka Doncic led the way with 28 points and eight assists , while Jake LaRavia delivered a strong double-double with 15 points and 10 rebounds. Walker Kessler added 10 points, 12 rebounds, and two blocks against his former team, and the Lakers also had solid bench production from Collin Sexton and Ziaire Williams. For Utah, Kyle Filipowski had an impressive performance with 21 points and 12 rebounds, while Ace Bailey contributed 18 points. However, the Jazz struggled mightily from three-point range, making just 6-32 attempts. Here are five takeaways from the Lakers’ victory. 1. Luka Doncic Led The Way Despite An Inefficient Shooting Night Doncic finished with 28 points, eight assists, four rebounds, and one steal, leading all scorers. However, this wasn’t necessarily one of his most efficient games. The Lakers superstar shot just 8-24 from the field (respect to Kobe Bryant?) and 3-14 from three-point range. Fortunately, he made nine of his 10 free throws, allowing him to reach 28 points despite struggling to find his rhythm from the perimeter. His playmaking remained important, as he tied Quentin Grimes for the team lead with eight assists. Doncic also finished with a plus-14 rating, showing that his overall impact extended beyond his shooting numbers. The encouraging part for Los Angeles is that it managed to win comfortably without needing an efficient scoring night from its best player. Doncic’s ability to get to the line and create opportunities for teammates helped keep the offense functioning. 2. Jake LaRavia And Walker Kessler Provided Massive Help LaRavia and Kessler were two of the biggest reasons Los Angeles controlled the game. LaRavia recorded 15 points and 10 rebounds, shooting 6-10 from the field. He also collected five offensive rebounds, giving the Lakers valuable second-chance opportunities. Kessler delivered an equally important performance inside, finishing with 10 points, 12 rebounds, one steal, and two blocks. He shot 4-5 from the field and grabbed eight defensive rebounds. The Lakers needed that interior production against a Utah team that finished with 46 rebounds and 60 points in the paint. Kessler’s rim protection and LaRavia’s activity helped prevent the Jazz from turning their size advantage into a decisive edge. Their contributions were especially important because Los Angeles didn’t dominate the glass, finishing with 45 rebounds compared to Utah’s 46. 3. item.title: Fani-Kayode denies recall, meets Enikanolaiye
item.description: Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has denied reports that he was recalled from his diplomatic posting, saying his visit to Abuja was to brief the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on his activities and consult with officials. Fani-Kayode spoke on Monday after meeting with the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Sola Enikanolaiye, at the ministry’s headquarters in Abuja. He said the meeting was part of his official responsibilities and had nothing to do with reports circulating on social media that he had been recalled. “There have been reports on social media suggesting that I have been recalled. Those claims are simply untrue. “If I had been recalled, I doubt I would be standing here smiling after a cordial and productive meeting with the minister,” he said. The envoy explained that his visit was to submit official reports, consult with ministry officials, spend time with his family and prepare for their possible relocation to South Africa. He said he had initially planned to spend only a few days in South Africa following his posting but had extended his stay to complete necessary diplomatic procedures. Fani-Kayode also dismissed reports that his meeting with South Africa’s Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) over the controversy surrounding the omission of his speech during the presentation of his letters of credence to President Cyril Ramaphosa amounted to a reprimand. He described the engagement as cordial and constructive, saying concerns were addressed professionally by both sides. “Our engagements with South African authorities have been cordial and constructive. Concerns have been raised on both sides in a professional diplomatic manner, and no reprimand of any kind occurred,” he said. The high commissioner reaffirmed his commitment to strengthening diplomatic relations between Nigeria and South Africa, particularly in trade, investment and other areas of mutual interest. “I believe strongly that if South Africa and Nigeria do not come together, it would affect the destiny of the whole African continent. We will do our best to build that bridge, and that bridge must never be broken,” he said. He, however, stressed that efforts to improve bilateral relations must not come at the expense of Nigeria’s national interests or the dignity, rights and welfare of Nigerians living in South Africa. Fani-Kayode expressed concern over persistent xenophobic attacks, killings and discriminatory rhetoric targeting Nigerians in the country. He also condemned attempts to portray Nigerians collectively as criminals and drug dealers, insisting that the actions of a few individuals should not be used to stigmatise an entire community. “As ambassador, I would be failing in my responsibility if I did not raise concerns about the treatment of Nigerians in South Africa. “Thousands of Nigerians in South Africa are law-abiding professionals, including doctors, lawyers, academics and entrepreneurs. item.title: Injury-hit PSG plotting winter swoop for RB Leipzig star Antonio Nusa
item.description: Injury-hit PSG plotting winter swoop for RB Leipzig star Antonio Nusa According to 'AS', Antonio Nusa of RB Leipzig fame is among the favorites for a move to Ligue 1 giants Paris Saint-Germain. PSG are forced to act in the winter transfer market after Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Désiré Doué both suffered a cruciate ligament tears. As a result new winger is desperately needed. The Norwegian is currently the Bundesliga's top provider with five goals and seven assists. Leipzig are reportedly demanding €80million for a summer sale and have previously stated their intentions to keep the Norwegian star . However, in mid-season and considering PSG 's precarious financial situation, RB Leipzig could tempted to demand a chunk more. According to AS, also on Paris Saint-Germain's shortlist are the likes of Gianluca Prestianni, Ibrahim Maza, Nico Williams and Estêvão. Other options include Julián Álvarez and Luis Díaz. However, Díaz is unlikely to be available; Bayern Munich need him desperately.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes’ Trainer Bobby Stroupe Fires Off 2-Word Message as Joe Burrow’s Bengals Fall to Commanders on MNF
item.description: Patrick Mahomes' Trainer Bobby Stroupe Fires Off 2-Word Message as Joe Burrow's Bengals Fall to Commanders on MNF A day after the Kansas City Chiefs took care of business and picked up a comfortable 34-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals, Patrick Mahomes’ trainer made it a point to keep an eye on the proceedings on Monday Night Football. With Joe Burrow firmly entrenched as one of the top contenders in the MVP race, all eyes were on whether he would pull a rabbit out of the hat during the Cincinnati Bengals’ primetime showdown against the Washington Commanders. Unfortunately for Burrow, the loss to Washington played completely into the hands of Mahomes, Josh Allen, and Brock Purdy, as the Bengals fell to a 22-20 loss. Bobby Stroupe’s 2-Word Post After Joe Burrow’s MNF Loss The Bengals’ loss came the day after Mahomes threw for 324 yards and three touchdowns in the Chiefs’ 34-7 rout of the Cardinals. Stroupe’s message read, in full, “Yeah boiiiiii,” and came just minutes after the Bengals fell to the Commanders in a thrilling MNF showdown that went right down to the wire. In fact, the Commanders’ game-winning 26-yard field goal came with just two seconds to spare. The day before, Mahomes carved up Arizona from the opening drive. He completed 27 of 39 passes without an interception and hit Travis Kelce for touchdowns of 8 and 22 yards and Xavier Worthy for an 18-yarder as Kansas City improved to 8-2. EVERY QB, GRADED: PFN’s NFL QB Impact Rankings In Week 11, Mahomes’ exploits landed him an 86.6 grade in PFN’s NFL QB Impact Metric, which ranks fourth of 26 graded quarterbacks. Burrow, meanwhile, got an 80.3 grade, which ranks seventh. Mahomes vs. Burrow Headlines NFL MVP Race The primary question after Week 11’s slate wrapped up was whether Burrow had done enough to stay atop the mountain in the MVP race . He finished his night going 28-of-40 for 300 yards and two touchdowns. PFN’s Jacob Infante believes this game will not exactly dent Burrow’s chances. “I don’t think this game will hurt Joe Burrow’s MVP candidacy all that much. He’s still clearly been a top performer at quarterback this season, and he performed well enough against the Commanders to stay highly ranked in PFN QB Impact grading, coming in second in the NFL,” Infante remarked after Monday Night Football. “He did what he had to do and got the Bengals into field goal range; it was the defense that didn’t get the job done.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Fellow PFN analyst Brandon Astreicher struck a similar tone, saying, “I don’t think Joe Burrow’s MVP case took that big of a hit tonight. While Burrow wasn’t as lights-out as he’s been for over a month, he played well, racked up some stats, and got Cincinnati the lead with under a minute to go. “But losing to the Commanders might have some thinking otherwise about his MVP campaign. Burrow is still my pick to win the award, but I’d have no problems if you have Brock Purdy just ahead of Burrow after tonight.” Chiefs H

item.title: Joe Burrow sends simple message after Bengals came up short vs. Commanders
item.description: Frank Bowen IV/The Enquirer / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Joe Burrow sends simple message after Bengals came up short vs. Commanders appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Joe Burrow did everything he could during Monday night’s Week 11 matchup against the Washington Commanders, but the Cincinnati Bengals defense ultimately failed to protect their chances of winning. Burrow appeared visibly frustrated while leaving the field after the Bengals suffered a heartbreaking defeat to Washington and later delivered a brief but honest assessment of his team’s performance. During his postgame press conference, Burrow admitted that the team’s performance was not good enough to get the job done. “Obviously not good enough to win,” Burrow said. “Just not good enough. We all can be better, for sure.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Burrow also acknowledged Washington’s defensive approach, giving credit to the Commanders for making things difficult for Cincinnati. “They do a good job, and they have good plans, and they’re going to do what they do, and they make it tough. If we get the first down, you know we don’t give them a chance to have the ball; one of them made a bad play, and the second one they covered it pretty well.” The defeat dropped the Bengals to a 7-3 record . However, Burrow once again delivered a stellar individual performance, completing 28 of 40 passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns despite the disappointing result. Head coach Zac Taylor also said that Cincinnati failed to perform at its best, particularly during the opening stages of the game. “Tough to find a rhythm early,” Taylor said. “Those first couple drives, obviously we weren’t at our best. They did a great job; they were aggressive. They took the fight to us a little bit. After that, I thought we found a really good rhythm the last two drives of the first half and coming out in the second half. We just weren’t able to finish there at the end of the game. Those last two drives are what got us.” The loss brought an end to Cincinnati’s five-game winning streak and also halted its franchise-record streak of scoring at least 30 points in five consecutive games. The Bengals will now look to bounce back when they return home to face the New Orleans Saints in Week 12. item.title: Chelsea defender recalls the horrors of facing Real Madrid in 2023: ‘It was crazy’
item.description: Chelsea defender recalls the horrors of facing Real Madrid in 2023: ‘It was crazy’ The UEFA Champions League has always been Real Madrid’s forte, and the men in white have almost always managed to find a way through the high-pressure encounters regardless of their form. Their dominance in the competition speaks for itself, especially over the past decade where their European success almost outweighs their domestic success. The 2022-23 season, however, was one rare campaign where Real Madrid themselves were handed a taste of their own medicine in the semifinal, where they faced a humiliating 5-1 defeat at the hands of Manchester City. Even in that season, however, they beat Chelsea by a dominant 4-0 scoreline on aggregate and showed their calibre to the world. Chelsea defender relives Real Madrid nightmare Speaking to the media in a recent interview, Wesley Fofana opened up on Real Madrid’s dominant win over Chelsea in the quarter-final of the 2023 UEFA Champions League and how Los Blancos were a class apart all over the field. Benzema was in surreal form. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) He began by praising the man who was on fire against them and inflicted most of the damage – Karim Benzema. “Quarter-final tie against Real Madrid: Let’s not talk about it, Karim Benzema traumatised me. He knocked us out on his own,” he began. “Him and Vini Jr, it was crazy,” Fofana added, crediting Vinicius Jr. for a great performance too. The defender was then asked about Rodrygo scoring a brace against them, but continued to insist that it was Vinicius and Benzema who took the tie away from them, not Rodrygo. “Rodrygo scored a brace? Rodrygo finished the job I guess, but I’m not talking about who scored the goals, I’m talking about football. “And talking about football, Vini Jr. and Benzema were too much, it made no sense,” he added. Chelsea never stood a chance. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Fofana then called Real Madrid’s 2023 a ‘dream’ team and also heaped praise on the midfield. “They and Modric too, they had a dream team.” Finally, he concluded by humbly admitting that his side stood no chance against Real Madrid at that point in time, saying, “We went to the Bernabéu, and they taught us a lesson. Vini was on fire and I had a bad night.” Source: Zack Nani TV

item.title: Old Trafford to potentially be part of global event to “inspire millions” across the world of women’s football
item.description: Old Trafford to potentially be part of global event to “inspire millions” across the world of women’s football Manchester United’s Old Trafford has been named as a potential candidate to host the Women’s World Cup in 2035. Hosts confirmed The Women’s World Cup will officially be held in England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland in 2035. The club’s official site has reported that “Manchester United has been confirmed as a candidate host venue for the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2035, after the announcement the tournament will be staged across the UK .” The website also adds that it is set to be “the biggest single-sport event held in the UK” and the first FIFA World Cup since 1966 to be held in the United Kingdom. The tournament will have 48 teams competing across 104 matches over 39 days. The event is expected to sell 4.5 million tickets and, with a projected global television audience of 3.5 billion, is likely to enthral fans around the world. Importantly, “the bid submission included Old Trafford in its current form, but the intention is for our new stadium to be considered for selection by FIFA once further details regarding the new development are confirmed.” Manchester United Chief Executive Officer Omar Berrada stated, “the Women’s World Cup in 2035 has the potential to be a transformative moment for women’s football, setting new standards for attendance, visibility and participation around the world. Bringing the tournament to the UK will create a significant opportunity to inspire millions of people and accelerate the growth of the game.” He also confirmed that United were “proud” to play their part in it and that the new 100,000 stadium will be designed to host “the biggest moments in global sport.” Finally, he explained, “hosting Women’s World Cup matches in our new stadium would be a fitting way to showcase Manchester and the women’s game on the world’s biggest stage.” Passed over Old Trafford has hosted international matches before, having hosted group matches in the 1966 World Cup and numerous matches, including the semi-final of Euro 1996. The stadium also held the Champions League final in 2003. Nonetheless, it was not selected as part of the UK and Ireland’s Euro 2028 bid. Featured image by Michael Regan via Getty Images online polls

item.title: Javier Mascherano reveals why Pep Guardiola turned him into a centre-back at Barcelona: ‘I ended up liking it’
item.description: Javier Mascherano reveals why Pep Guardiola turned him into a centre-back at Barcelona: ‘I ended up liking it’ Javier Mascherano has explained how Pep Guardiola changed the course of his Barcelona career by converting him from a defensive midfielder into a centre-back, a positional adjustment that ultimately allowed him to establish himself at the Camp Nou. The Argentine arrived from Liverpool in 2010 as competition for Sergio Busquets, but defensive injuries and Guardiola’s tactical decisions gradually gave him a new role that became central to his success in Catalonia. Mascherano has now reflected on the reasoning behind the switch, admitting that adapting to an unfamiliar position was essential to earning regular opportunities in one of the strongest Barcelona teams in the club’s history. Guardiola’s decision gave Mascherano a route into the starting XI Mascherano initially faced a difficult situation competing with Busquets for the defensive midfield position. Rather than displacing the established Spain international, Guardiola explored the possibility of using the Argentine in central defence. The circumstances also favoured the experiment, as Carles Puyol’s knee problems and Eric Abidal’s serious health issues left Barcelona short of defensive options, creating an opportunity for Mascherano to demonstrate his versatility. His first centre-back appearance came against Almeria before Guardiola selected him in defence for the Champions League trip to Shakhtar Donetsk in April 2011. Javier Mascherano signed for Barcelona in 2010. (Photo by Manuel Queimadelos Alonso/Getty Images) Mascherano explained the manager’s thinking behind the decision, stating, “When I arrived at Barça, I was clearly a pivot. But in that position, it was either Sergio Busquets or me. “I imagine Guardiola thought that instead of moving the best player in his position, he would move the other one. That’s how I started playing as a centre-back, and I ended up liking it,” he explained. Mascherano embraced the challenge of changing positions The former Argentina international acknowledged that accepting a different role was an important part of his development. Rather than seeing the positional change as an obstacle, he recognised that adapting gave him a better chance of staying in Guardiola’s plans. “That’s part of a footballer’s evolution: understanding that you have very little chance of playing regularly in a certain position and being willing to adapt. “I found my place in defence, embraced the opportunity, and fought to earn more minutes,” he added. Javier Mascherano was initially signed to compete with Sergio Busquets. (Photo by Nils Petter Nilsson/Ombrello/Getty Images) Notably, his transition also demanded an understanding of Barcelona’s defensive requirements. Playing under Guardiola meant contributing to possession, building attacks from the back and maintaining positional discipline rather than concentrating primarily on defensive recovery. item.title: Hey, Zac Taylor, Joe Burrow. What happened to running the ball?
item.description: The Cincinnati Bengals are a solid team. They're capable of being great. But they simply refuse to commit to what it takes to achieve greatness. Run. The. Damn. Ball. No thanks, says Zac Taylor and Joe Burrow . Be it the head coach's stubbornness or the quarterback's arrogance – or vice versa – the Bengals just won't commit to running the ball even when the game situation calls for it. And their refusal to run the ball and control the clock late in the game cost the Bengals in a 22-20 loss to the Washington Commanders on Oct. 23 at rain-soaked Northwest Stadium in suburban D.C. It was Cincinnati's first loss since Oct. 4 vs. Jacksonville. Remember what happened that day? The Bengals refused to run the ball. Mark the Washington game down as another example of why the Bengals probably aren't going to win the Super Bowl this season. If ever there was a game to run the ball more, it was on a wet and windy night against a gritty but inferior opponent. But Taylor and Burrow couldn't be bothered to run a balanced offense. It's like they can't help themselves. They insist on showing the world on almost every play that the Bengals are a great passing team, even though everyone already knows that. The Bengals ran the ball one time in the fourth quarter, failing to protect a one-point lead and milk the clock. Cincinnati held a 17-16 lead when it took possession of the ball with 10:27 remaining. Burrow proceeded to throw the ball five times for 23 yards. No running plays. The Bengals only ate up 2 minutes and 2 seconds before having to punt. A run play or two could've taken, say, an extra 46 seconds off the clock. The Bengals again had the opportunity to run the ball on their last possession and take the clock down to 4 or 5 seconds to set up what should've been a game-winning field goal. First, Burrow connected with Mike Gesicki on a 32-yard pass to set up the Bengals with a first down at the Washington 32-yard line. Perfect. That pass should've set up three straight run plays, right? Next play: 3-yard run by Samaje Perine, forcing Washington to take its second timeout. Good. But then Burrow inexplicably dropped back to pass on second down. The pass was nearly intercepted. It stopped the clock. The Bengals got bailed out because a Commanders player was slow to get up, forcing Washington to call its last timeout. Then Burrow dropped back to pass on third down and got sacked, nearly putting the Bengals out of field-goal range. What?! Instead, there was 46 seconds left on the clock after Evan McPherson drilled a 56-yard field goal. No one should blame the Bengals' defense for allowing the two big pass plays to set up Washington's game-winning field goal. The defense played well. It gave up one touchdown all game. It was the type of defensive performance Bengals fans were clamoring for the last two seasons. Some of the guys the Bengals picked up in the offseason to bolster the defense were outstanding, including three sacks by Boye Mafe. No, this loss is on Tay

item.title: Predators’ Struggle to Recapture Early Season Power-Play Success
item.description: Jonathan Marchesault and Filip Forsberg celebrate goal against Ottowa October 2026 Getty The Nashville Predators were a top-three team in power-play percentage throughout October, but have since hit a cold spell this month. The Preds had a 33.3% power-play percentage at their peak in October, ranking them third-best in the NHL. Since then, they have steadily fallen, going just 4-for-30 over their last 30 power-play opportunities and dropping to ninth in the NHL (24.7%). The Predators’ Power Play Nashville’s primary power play unit consists of Steven Stamkos, Ryan O’Reilly, Jonathan Marchessault, Roman Josi and Filip Forsberg. On paper, the five make perfect sense, comprising four of the team’s top five players in points , with the outlier being Marchessault, who missed two weeks with an injury and still ranks seventh. The rotation worked perfectly in October as well, helping keep them near the top of the Central Division, where they currently reside. The goal-scoring ability of Steven Stamkos, who sits fifth all-time in power-play goals scored , paired with the veteran playmaking of Forsberg, O’Reilly, and Josi, was extremely efficient, but that production hasn’t been there of late. Stamkos has been the only power-play goal scorer on the team in November, as the Predators have gone 3-25 on opportunities (12%), putting them in the bottom five for the month . Still sitting at 12-6-5 on the year, the Predators have managed to succeed despite their recently slumping power play, winning six straight to start the month of November. However, power plays are an important part of a team’s success, as consistently scoring with the man advantage is almost required for any playoff-contending team. What Needs to Change With the amount of top-heavy veteran experience on the Predators’ roster, it seems they might just have to ride out the slump and hope the power play finds its way back. Currently still the ninth-best in the NHL, Nashville knows its power play was once one of its strongest aspects. However, since then, the defense has stepped up while the power play has gone ghost. Filled with veterans providing a large majority of the team’s points, Nashville has to keep its faith in them and hope they can begin to click again. Breaking the slump starts with getting Marchessault more involved and continuing to feed the historically prolific power-play scorer, Steven Stamkos. The return of Jonathan Marchessault has been a recent boost to the offense with a goal in each of his last two games , and Nashville will need him to bring that same impact to its 5-on-4 play to get back to full power. Currently sitting tied for third in the Central Division in points, Nashville could put itself in a key position to snap its two-year playoff drought if it can return to a top-five power play while retaining its recent defensive and goaltending strengths. item.title: ‘Troy (Aikman) Is Going Back to FOX Sports,’ ‘Looks Miserable’ — NFL Fans Take Notice of Cowboys Legend’s ‘Tension’ With Joe Buck on ESPN’s MNF
item.description: ‘Troy (Aikman) Is Going Back to FOX Sports,’ ‘Looks Miserable’ — NFL Fans Take Notice of Cowboys Legend’s ‘Tension’ With Joe Buck on ESPN’s MNF The Troy Aikman-Joe Buck saga on ESPN’s “Monday Night Football” just keeps rolling. Aikman still has no deal beyond this season, and ESPN has already given Buck a new contract. Aikman was reportedly part of a tense confrontation with his broadcast partner over the situation, and he has since joked that Buck always wanted a “one-man booth.” With so much simmering behind the scenes, fans have been watching the two closely for any sign of strain. In Week 11, as the Washington Commanders hosted the Cincinnati Bengals, several viewers thought they spotted it again on the air. Fans Think Troy Aikman Looks Unhappy on MNF Broadcast With Joe Buck The saga has escalated over multiple weeks between Aikman, Buck and ESPN. The two have called games together for more than two decades and joined the network in 2022 on five-year deals. Those deals expire after the 2026 season. Buck reportedly signed a new contract this offseason, while Aikman, a three-time Super Bowl champion, has yet to be offered one. That has created friction among everyone involved. More than a month ago, in a verbal altercation , Aikman reportedly blamed Buck for his lack of a new contract. Buck flatly denied responsibility in that exchange. Since then, fans have spotted signs of dysfunction between the two on air, and it was most apparent in Week 11. “Troy Aikman shooting daggers at Joe Buck,” one fan wrote , posting a video of the game’s intro in which Buck welcomes viewers while Aikman looks low on energy. Another fan mocked the pair , “Lmao, Joe Buck and Troy Aikman, the country knows there’s beef, but they have to sit there and talk like everything is gravy. This is too funny.” A third fan wrote , “Boy, you can SEE the tension and FEEL it in the booth with Troy Aikman and Joe Buck. This thing is OVER. item.title: Why Commanders’ Jayden Daniels ‘lives’ for game-winning drives like MNF win over Bengals
item.description: Jeffrey Becker-Imagn Images Why Commanders’ Jayden Daniels ‘lives’ for game-winning drives like MNF win over Bengals appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jayden Daniels doesn’t just survive pressure when games hang in the balance. He embraces the pressure and thrives in it. The Washington Commanders quarterback has quickly developed a reputation for delivering when the stakes are highest. Monday night’s thrilling comeback against the Cincinnati Bengals was another reminder of why he thrives in those moments. With Washington trailing and less than a minute remaining, Daniels orchestrated a game-winning drive with remarkable composure. It reinforced the belief that the Commanders are never truly out of a game with No. 5 under center. Speaking after Washington’s 22-20 Monday Night Football upset win in Week 11, Daniels explained why situations like these are precisely what he lives for . “I personally live for those moments.” 😤 Jayden Daniels on the Commanders game-winning drive. pic.twitter.com/dQJcPPteDj Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — NFL Network (@nflnetwork) November 24, 2026 “I personally live for those moments,” Daniels said via NFL Network. “Those are the moments you dream about as a kid—being down late, two-minute drill, trusting your guys, and going down to win the game.” Daniels certainly delivered on that sentiment against Cincinnati. The Commanders trailed 20-19 with just 46 seconds left. He then engineered a three-play, 64-yard drive. Daniels connected with breakout wide receiver Antonio Williams on a crucial pass before Drew Stevens drilled the walk-off 26-yard field goal. Daniels finished with 289 passing yards and another 55 on the ground. He also did not commit a turnover, despite Washington missing top receiver Terry McLaurin. Through 11 weeks, Daniels has thrown for 1,788 yards and 10 touchdowns against just two interceptions. He has also added 335 rushing yards and two scores. After missing Weeks 3 and 4 with an injury, he has helped spark Washington’s turnaround. Now 4-5-1 and riding consecutive victories , the Commanders are back in the NFC East conversation. Daniels’ confidence and ability to deliver under pressure should prove pivotal down the stretch. item.title: Why has De Bruyne struggled at Napoli as he returns to Man City?
item.description: Kevin de Bruyne won 16 trophies in 10 years at Manchester City [Getty Images] Kevin de Bruyne's move to Napoli in 2025 was supposed to mark a continuation of his glittering decade at Manchester City as he approaches the twilight years of his career. Instead, the midfielder, who is widely regarded as one of the stand-out players of his generation, has seen his time in Naples threaten to turn sour amid an early injury, friction with his team-mates and rumours of a January exit. Napoli were Serie A champions in 2024-25 - the year before De Bruyne's arrival - but are currently languishing in eighth, while they sit 27th in the Champions League after a heavy 4-1 defeat at Porto earlier this month. Belgium international De Bruyne lifted 16 trophies in his 10 years at City and is guaranteed a generous ovation when he returns to the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday but the highs of his time in England are in contrast to the struggles he is seemingly enduring in Italy. "Not a lot I can say for the moment," said De Bruyne when asked about his future. "I have played at 100% until now and obviously I am not 20 years old, I am turning 36. "There is a lot of things going in my mind but there is not a lot to say. I am playing good football, trying to help the team to do well and it has been a bit of a challenging season with a lot of things happening." De Bruyne's feelings for Man City will 'never change' Did Man City let De Bruyne leave too soon? Statue, Pep's tears & a missed sitter - De Bruyne's emotional farewell 'A bad show' in quarrel with team-mate City decided not to renew De Bruyne's contract during the 2024-25 season and the player had the choice of heading to the US with Chicago Fire or staying in one of the top-five leagues in Europe. The 35-year-old felt he could still cut it at the highest level but his first season at Napoli was heavily disrupted by a hamstring injury which kept him out for more than four months, restricting him to 21 appearances. Napoli finished runners up to Inter Milan to lose their Serie A title and De Bruyne reportedly said he was "happy" manager Antonio Conte had departed in the summer as promises were not kept regarding the style of play. But despite making his name as a technically gifted number 10, De Bruyne's role has been remodelled into a deeper holding one under Massimiliano Allegri in an ageing squad that has struggled this season. In Porto, the fractures were clear to see, with De Bruyne having a heated on-field confrontation with striker Lorenzo Lucca and his team-mates were forced to step in to diffuse the situation. The passionate side of De Bruyne's game was shown in Manchester too. The midfielder shouted "shut up" at manager Pep Guardiola during a Champions League game against Real Madrid in 2023, and said "let me talk" when David Silva and Fernandinho were ushering him off the pitch at half-time shortly after he was booked against Napoli in 2017.
