item.title: Why Commanders’ MNF win over Bengals feels so good to Jacory Croskey-Merritt
item.description: © Amber Searls-Imagn Images Why Commanders’ MNF win over Bengals feels so good to Jacory Croskey-Merritt appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jacory Croskey-Merritt returned from injured reserve Monday night and scored the Washington Commanders ’ only touchdown in a 22-20 win over the Cincinnati Bengals. What stuck with him afterward was how much work went into a result that came down to the final kick. The Commanders activated the second-year running back earlier Monday after he missed four games with a groin injury. He carried 13 times for 54 yards and caught two passes for 23 yards. His 1-yard touchdown cut the Bengals’ lead to 10-7 in the second quarter at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Maryland. NFL Network shared a clip from Croskey-Merritt’s postgame press conference Monday on X, formerly Twitter. Still in his No. 22 jersey, he explained why the win felt so good. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “We put so much time in it, so it always feels good to get the outcome that you want.” Bill with a sigh of relief after the Commanders wild MNF win 😅 pic.twitter.com/mAX7zIIiF3 — NFL Network (@nflnetwork) November 24, 2026 Washington rushed for 150 yards, including 55 from quarterback Jayden Daniels , but needed two big plays through the air to win. Evan McPherson’s 56-yard field goal put Cincinnati ahead 20-19. The Commanders got the ball back with 39 seconds left and no timeouts. Daniels found rookie receiver Antonio Williams for 22 yards, spiked the ball, then went back to Williams for a 42-yard gain to the Bengals’ 8-yard line. Daniels spiked the ball again with five seconds left, and Drew Stevens made the 26-yard winner as time expired for his fifth field goal of the night. The Commanders improved to 4-5-1 with their third win in four games and stayed within two games of the division-leading New York Giants in the NFC East. The last-second defeat snapped the Bengals’ five-game winning streak and dropped them to 7-3. item.title: Everton Player Ratings vs Brentford: Dismal Day For The Toffees
item.description: Rating the players after that game is a difficult task, that's for sure. It was a dismal evening for Everton , succumbing to a 4-0 defeat against Brentford , and deservedly so too. James Tarkowski's red card undoubtedly had a big impact on the game, but Everton looked down and out before that. Brentford were deservedly ahead before Tarkowski was given his marching orders, and it was a huge mountain to climb from then. Even with seven players ruled out , including striker Igor Thiago, Everton failed to show up. Onto the player ratings. Jordan Pickford - 5 Poor distribution and maybe could have done something for the fourth goal, but about five players all deserve some blame for that. Couldn't do anything about the other three goals, though, so feels harsh to rate him lower than that. Jake O’Brien - 4 Sloppy in possession, poor for the fourth goal, and just overall not at the races. Certainly hinders us going forward when he plays at right-back. James Tarkowski - 2 We can argue all day about whether it’s a red card, and I’m sure we will for a few days to come, but it’s a silly challenge to make. Tarkowski does that regularly, following through on a tackle. In this day and age, you are asking for trouble, and he let his team down not only for the Brentford game, but for Sunday as well. Jarrad Branthwaite - 5 Thought he dealt with a lot aerially throughout the game. 17 defensive contributions. One of those who could have done better for the fourth, unfortunate with another deflected goal. IMAGO / APL Not his best performance, but not a player to point fingers at. Vitalii Mykolenko - 5 Booked early on for a foul that led to one of the goals. Wasn’t awful outside of that, and it was a difficult evening for the defence from minute one. James Garner - 3 A lot of contributions defensively but it’s so often recovering after being out of position. Didn’t impact the game in possession and Brentford found it way too easy to play through our midfield. Many point to his defensive contributions to suggest that he’s a strong player out of possession, but he’s part of a midfield structure that struggles consistently. Harrison Armstrong - 4 Honestly felt like he hardly touched the ball, and when he did, he didn’t look after it too well. Covered ground as usual, but offered very little in possession, and again, our midfield was all over the place. Merlin Rohl - 2 A really poor performance from Rohl. Possibly Everton’s worst player. Offered us nothing going forward, struggled to keep possession, and didn’t provide enough cover defensively to justify playing a more defensive player on the right-hand side. IMAGO / APL Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall - 4 Felt a bit sorry for him and Thierno Barry after the red card as it was a thankless task. Despite that, Dewsbury-Hall was poor before the red card too. Very sloppy in possession and didn’t impact the game positively at all. Thierno Barry - 4 Feel harsh rating him this low as it was a horrible game for him. Ball lumped up to him w

item.title: There is a bonafide defence for Enzo Maresca as his Manchester City side has hit a road bump
item.description: There is a bonafide defence for Enzo Maresca as his Manchester City side has hit a road bump In portions of the frustrating 1-1 draw that Manchester City had with Fulham, the frustration of the Etihad Stadium crowd was impossible to ignore. Boos rang out at times when Enzo Maresca’s side failed to press Fulham and the entire game felt passive on occasions. Watching the City players out of possession, they did seem confused with their manager’s expectations in such scenarios. While it was a jarring sight, it does speak to the upheaval process that Manchester City are undertaking under Enzo Maresca. Pep Guardiola was Manchester City’s figurehead and manager for the past decade. Given the way City played under Guardiola, it was almost taken for granted how his team would play and perform in each and every match. But, a significant change has occurred at City and that security blanket has been removed. Enzo Maresca described the task he and his team are facing yesterday and it was a valid point that Maresca raised. Speaking yesterday, Enzo Maresca explained that he is still trying to find the right balance for his Manchester City team. Enzo Maresca faced the media yesterday ahead of Manchester City’s UEFA Champions League league phase fixture against Napoli. The Manchester City manager explained that he is still trying to find the right balance for his team. Manchester City’s midfield remains a work in progress as does City’s defence and attack. Maresca explained yesterday: “ It’s just a matter to know each other, I need to understand how is the idea one for these kind of games, the idea one for different kinds of games. I don’t think it’s just midfield, also we are trying with defensive players to find the right solution. ” “ Again, it’s for me part of the process because we need… It’s like a reset, a restart, after 10 years with the same manager, same face, same words, same method. It’s not easy to all of sudden change. ” “ For me personally, it’s all normal, and hopefully as soon as possible we can find the right balance in all the lines – defensive, midfield – and we can be consistent, which for me is the difference between us and other clubs. ” Everything is new at City under Maresca and that can be glossed over at times. It may be unpopular at the moment to defend Enzo Maresca, but he is right. The size of the rebuild at Manchester City is sizable. No manager can come in and pick up where Pep Guardiola left off. Expecting that to take place is doomed to failure. Guardiola is a one-of-a-kind manager and his demands and standards were set in stone. It almost became a surprise when City played outside the norm under Guardiola. Such was the high standards of performance and results he established during his decade as City manager. However, Enzo Maresca’s Manchester City side is a work in progress. There will be fluctuations in performance as Maresca looks to find the right balance with his lineups. item.title: Lauren Whittaker Elected to North Shore Showcase All-Tournament Team
item.description: Feb 26, 2026; Spokane, Washington, USA; Gonzaga Bulldogs forward Lauren Whittaker (33) is introduced before a game against the Saint Mary's Gaels at McCarthey Athletic Center. Mandatory Credit: James Snook-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Despite only finishing with a 1-1 outcome in Laie, Hawaii, it was another awe-inspiring stretch of performances for Gonzaga Bulldogs redshirt sophomore forward Lauren Whittaker. She was named to the North Shore Showcase All-Tournament Team along with the Most Valuable Player, California Golden Bears senior guard Shannon Dowell. In Game 1’s too-close-for-comfort 63-57 victory over the host Hawaii Rainbow Wahine, the 6-3 Kiwi ended up with 14 points on 7-for-16 shooting, 14 rebounds, and two steals. As for Game 2’s 71-60 loss to the undefeated Golden Bears at 7-0, Whittaker added 20 points on 6-for-15 field goals, 13 rebounds, and five assists/two turnovers. The Zags left their trip with a 4-4 overall record. All-tournament honors for Whitty 👏 pic.twitter.com/i46Ev95432 — Gonzaga Women's Basketball (@ZagWBB) November 24, 2026 In the 2026-27 season, the Gonzaga leader down inside the paint has already collected four double-doubles (tied for No. 4 in the nation) and grabs 10.4 rebounds per game (tied for No. 22 in the country). Whittaker hasn’t missed a beat coming off her coming-out party in the 2025-26 campaign and continues to stuff the stat sheet. Next for the Zags is a return home to the Inland Northwest with a matchup against the Eastern Washington Eagles in nearby Cheney, Washington. Tip-off time is set for 2 p.m. PT on Sunday, Nov. 29, on SWX. Arden Cravalho is a Gonzaga University graduate from the Bay Area… Follow him on X @a_cravalho

item.title: It was an attempt on my life — Omo-Agege
item.description: Senator Omo-Agege, has alleged that the attack on his campaign train in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State was “premeditated”, saying it was part of an ongoing attempt to eliminate him. Speaking on Channels TV via Zoom, Omo-Agege said four members of his campaign organisation were killed, while about 15 others were critically injured when gunmen opened fire during his campaign event in Udu-Ere, Ughelli North. He said he was addressing supporters when the gunmen opened fire, adding that he heard them repeatedly shouting that they wanted to kill him. He said he survived the attack through the intervention of his Department of State Services, DSS, security details. He said the attack occurred less than five minutes after he began his remarks at the campaign venue. His words: “This is premeditated. It is not something that just happened today. I just gave you the buildup. This thing has been going on. “As I was speaking, I just moved over to the side of a vehicle to be able to make eye contact with those I was speaking with. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started. The former Deputy Senate President said four members of his campaign organisation were killed in the attack, including former Federal Character Commissioner, and the immediate past president of the Urhobo Progress Union youth wing. The former senator said he heard the attackers shouting in English, “Omo-Agege, we want to kill,” while the shooting was ongoing. Omo-Agege called on the Inspector-General of Police to take over the investigation, saying he did not expect the Delta State Police Command to deliver justice. “We are appealing to the IGP to step in immediately and directly handle this investigation. We need justice,” he said. We need justice. We need justice for these four people who have been killed. We need justice for the 15 people who are critically injured and hospitalised right now,” he said. He also appealed to his supporters not to retaliate, saying the attack would not deter him from continuing his campaign. “If the idea is that this is supposed to deter me from going forward with the campaigns, it’s a very, very big mistake and a big lie. It ain’t going to happen,” Omo-Agege said. The post It was an attempt on my life — Omo-Agege appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Police arrest eight suspected drug dealers in Jigawa
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The Jigawa State Police Command has arrested eight suspected drug dealers and consumers, including two women aged 18 and 20, during operations targeting illicit drug trafficking and substance abuse across the state. The arrests were disclosed in a statement issued to newsmen by the Police Public Relations Officer, SP Shiisu Lawan Adam. Adam identified the suspects as Garba Sabo, 20; Kamal Ibrahim, 20; Muhammad Ibrahim, 25; Muhammad Nura, 25; Muhammad Bako, 25; Habu Usman, 23, also known as Makwa; Firdausi Sani, 20; and Nusaiba Ibrahim, 18. According to the statement, the suspects, aged between 18 and 25, were arrested at different locations, including Gadama, Bulangu, Sara, Gumel and Kazaure towns. One of the female suspects was identified as a resident of Sandamu Daura in Katsina State. During the operations, the police recovered 8,739 assorted illicit drug-related substances, including suspected Indian hemp, tramadol, pregabalin, diazepam and other intoxicating substances. The recovered exhibits included 4,035 pieces of Exol, 1,384 pieces of D5, 634 pregabalin capsules, 896 tramadol capsules, 248 diazepam tablets and 1,199 wraps of marijuana, alongside three and a half blocks of the substance. Other items recovered included rubber solution, whisky, shisha, syrups, snuff and other intoxicating substances. The Commissioner of Police, CP Tijjani Murtala, said the command would sustain its operations against drug trafficking and substance abuse, warning those involved in the illicit trade to desist or face prosecution. He said the police would continue to deploy intelligence-led policing, surveillance and targeted operations to dismantle drug distribution networks and tackle criminal activities associated with substance abuse. The commissioner also called on parents, guardians, community leaders and religious institutions to intensify efforts to discourage drug abuse, particularly among young people. He urged members of the public to support the police in the fight against drug-related activities across the state. The post Police arrest eight suspected drug dealers in Jigawa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: INEC not anticipating technical glitches in 2027 — Abia REC
item.description: …Says commission building ICT facility, procuring equipment to prevent glitches …Gives Abia’s total registered voters as 2.62m …Explains why INEC relies on federal university VCs for collation, returning officers …Rules out owing ad-hoc staff allowances By Steve Oko The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has assured voters in Abia State that their votes will count in the 2027 general elections, declaring that the commission is putting necessary measures in place to deliver a free, fair, credible and seamless exercise. The Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Abia State, Professor Sylvia Uchenna Agu, gave the assurance in an exclusive interview with Vanguard, disclosing that the commission had commenced the receipt of non-sensitive election materials, including generators and brand-new Hilux vans, from its headquarters in Abuja. Agu, who assumed office in April, also spoke on the commission’s efforts to address infrastructural deficiencies at its Abia office, prevent a recurrence of the electronic transmission controversy, popularly known as the ‘technical glitch’, during the 2023 presidential election, ensure credible recruitment of ad-hoc personnel and improve election logistics. She disclosed that Abia’s voter register had increased from 2,180,140 in 2023 to 2,620,151, following the registration of 460,011 additional voters in the last Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise. The REC also explained why INEC relies heavily on federal universities in recruiting collation and returning officers, defended the commission’s use of other categories of ad-hoc personnel and urged eligible voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs). Excerpts: The 2027 general elections are approaching. How prepared is INEC in Abia State for the exercise? We are very much prepared. By the grace of God, we are still receiving our non-sensitive election materials. We have received generators, vehicles and other materials. For the first time, we have received brand-new Hilux vans, and more vehicles are expected in the coming days. Preparations are on top gear. On a weekly basis, we receive materials from Abuja, and the commission is making every effort to ensure that we deliver a seamless election. I can assure you that we are working towards a very successful election in 2027. You mentioned receiving new vehicles and other materials. But what is the state of your operational facilities in Abia, particularly your ICT infrastructure, which is critical to election management? When I assumed office in April, I was not impressed with what I saw. The condition of the facility was not encouraging. Sensitive materials, including result sheets for the local government areas, were packed in Ghana-Must-Go bags. There were no proper cabinets for storing them. item.title: Troops kill two bandits, recover rifles in Kogi operation
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Nigerian Army have neutralised two armed bandits and recovered two AK-47 rifles and other items during an intelligence-led ambush operation in Asungwe Forest, Okehi Local Government Area of Kogi State. According to a statement by Col. Appolonia Anele, the operation followed sustained offensives against banditry and kidnapping gangs in the state. The statement said the operation was conducted on Monday, November 23, 2026, by troops of the 12 Brigade under Operation Bem Hembe, in conjunction with other hybrid forces. It added that the operation was launched following credible intelligence obtained from previously arrested bandits, which provided actionable leads on the movement of criminal elements operating in Asungwe Forest and adjoining communities along the boundaries of Kogi, Edo and Ondo states. Acting on the intelligence, troops deployed from Patrol Base Kabba and positioned themselves along a suspected bandits’ crossing route within the forest. The troops subsequently made contact with the criminals and engaged them with superior firepower, neutralising two bandits, while others fled. Items recovered during the operation included two AK-47 rifles, three magazines, 27 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition, two Android phones, three Tecno keypad phones, assorted drugs and bags suspected to belong to the fleeing criminals. The statement said the operation demonstrated the Nigerian Army’s resolve to dismantle criminal networks, disrupt bandits’ movements and deny terrorists and kidnappers freedom of action across vulnerable communities. It added that the Army remained committed to intensifying intelligence-driven operations and sustaining pressure on criminal elements to enhance the security of lives and property. The Army also urged members of the public to continue providing credible and timely information to security agencies to support ongoing operations against criminal activities. item.title: Season’s sweat up in flames as fire ravages Yobe farms
item.description: By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman For four farmers in Gadana, months of labour and the promise of a rewarding harvest ended in ashes when fire swept through their farmlands, destroying approximately 147 bags of mature sorghum just weeks before the end of the year. In neighbouring communities, the devastation has taken different forms: two households in Godowoli have lost agricultural produce reserved to feed their families, while a tailor in Old Nangere has watched his sewing machines, fabrics, customers’ clothes and other tools of trade disappear in a fire that has crippled his business. The three incidents, recorded across Nangere and Fika Local Government Areas of Yobe State within five days, have left affected residents counting their losses, with 27 people in Nangere alone facing food insecurity, loss of income and economic hardship. The incidents were reported in two separate statements published on the official Facebook page of the Yobe State Emergency Management Agency (YOSEMA), both signed by its Director of Search and Rescue Operations, Dr M. I. Jalo. According to the agency, the first incident occurred at about 4pm on November 14 in Godowoli community, Nangere Ward, where fire destroyed harvested agricultural produce stored by two households as food reserves for the year. Four days later, another fire outbreak engulfed a tailoring shop in Old Nangere, destroying two electric sewing machines, electric irons, fabrics, customers’ clothes and other tailoring equipment. Beyond the immediate financial loss, the destruction has left the tailor without essential tools for his trade, while the loss of customers’ clothing could expose him to additional financial obligations. Midnight fire In Gadana farmland area of Fika Local Government Area, the fire outbreak occurred at about 1am on November 15, destroying mature sorghum crops belonging to four farmers. A joint assessment team comprising officials of the Local Emergency Management Committee, Community Development Officers and the affected farmers visited the farmlands to establish the extent of the damage. The assessment confirmed that approximately 147 bags of sorghum were lost, with the agency describing the destroyed crops as the major source of food, income and household sustenance for the affected farmers and their dependants. The agency said a detailed assessment documenting the affected farmers, farm sizes, estimated crop losses and corresponding financial implications had been compiled for consideration. For the affected households, the losses come with concerns about how to meet basic needs and sustain their livelihoods, particularly as the year draws to a close. YOSEMA said the affected farming community had appealed for urgent intervention to cushion the impact of the disaster, while expressing appreciation for the agency’s commitment to disaster risk management and emergency response. item.title: Omo Agege attack: Slain supporter was father of 6-month-old baby
item.description: By Efe Onodjae One of the supporters killed in the alleged assassination attempt on former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, was a father of just six months, having welcomed his first child on May 15, 2026. The deceased, identified as Efemena Umukoro, had taken to Facebook on May 15 to announce the birth of his baby boy, celebrating the safe delivery of his wife and child. In the emotional post, Umukoro narrated his experience during his wife’s labour, describing women as heroes for enduring the pains of childbirth. Sadly, six months after celebrating the arrival of his newborn son, Umukoro was found dead in his Toyota Highlander SUV following the alleged assassination attempt during a campaign tour by Omo-Agege in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. In a video seen by Vanguard, Umukoro was found lying lifeless in the vehicle, dressed in a white shirt and black shorts. Four persons were confirmed dead in the attack, which occurred during a political campaign activity in the community. In his May 15 Facebook post announcing the birth of his son, Umukoro wrote: “My Prince is here, mother and child in good health. Women are the heroes and keepers of life. “From 1cm to 10cm dilation, I stood firmly beside her through every painful minute that almost felt like a whole year suspended in time between hope and fear. “Indeed, women are heroes. They carry the deepest pains of this world in silence and strength. “I watched my beautiful wife grumble and tremble in agony, entering a realm where shame no longer existed. She tore off her clothes, choosing nakedness as though, in that vulnerable state, she found the strength to fight a battle nature designed only for mothers. “Every single minute mattered to us. I kept staring at my phone, counting contractions, wishing with all my heart that I could take the pain away from her. But each time I thought the worst had passed, the pain returned even harder. And there I was… helpless, watching the woman I love fight a war I could not fight for her. “How does one endure pain without knowing its limits? “How does a human body survive waves of agony with no certainty of when relief will finally come? The post Omo Agege attack: Slain supporter was father of 6-month-old baby appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Orgs that leak data ‘prioritize corporate interests over customers’ says Have I Been Pwned’s Troy Hunt
item.description: Troy Hunt, the founder of data breach reporting site Have I Been Pwned (HIBP), has revealed how organizations respond when he informs them they’ve leaked data – if they respond at all. Hunt gave Anthropic’s Claude access to an email inbox containing over eight years of his email correspondence and then asked the AI to write a post summarising them, a method he said “was the best way to highlight the behaviors I keep seeing across many breaches and subsequent disclosure efforts.” Writing in person, Hunt described those behaviors as “standoffish behavior, deliberate delays, heavy involvement from lawyers, and a constant theme: prioritizing corporate interests over those of their customers.” Once Claude takes over writing duties, it opens with the observation that Hunt sent his standard notification email to 73 organizations between March 2018 and November 2026 and also used website contact forms. Claude/Hunt focuses on the breach notifications that don’t go well, for example when first contact “often goes nowhere” because “many organisations have no obvious way to report a security incident.” Some organizations Hunt contacted logged his notifications as customer support requests. “In one case, Troy received three automated surveys asking him to rate the support he'd received,” Claude wrote, before observing “A message that an organization’s customer data is being traded among criminals ended up in the same queue as a question about a late delivery.” Once someone at victim organization gets the message, a common response is to say they can find no evidence of the breach. Others try to play down the incident, saying it was only a website defacement or that Hunt is re-reporting a previous breach the victim has already disclosed. If an organization accepts Hunt is probably onto something, it typically says it needs to investigate the matter. Claude’s take on Hunt’s mails suggests he responds by pointing out that this is an irresponsible approach, because while the investigation takes place, “people whose data has been taken don't know they need to change a password or watch for phishing.” Next, victims send in the lawyers who ask if their employer or client is legally required to reveal the breach. Hunt typically replies by saying it is up to the victim to decide if the incident meets the threshold that triggers mandatory disclosure requirements under local laws, but that he intends to notify HIBP users regardless. Victims don’t like hearing that and respond in three ways: Calling to discuss disclosure, rather than committing to it; Asking to see the wording HIBP will use in its disclosure, a request that sees Hunt refer the victim to the HIBP site for examples of the thousand-plus breach reports already on the site; Arguing that disclosure, not the breach, is the real harm. Hunt/Claude suggests that each argument victims use to avoid disclosure “sounds reasonable on its own,” but argues “Together, they mean the people most affected by the breach are t

item.title: Nigeria’s electricity crisis to persist as FG shifts debt payment to 2027
item.description: •Poor teamwork, illiquidity, others undermine efficiency – Tegbe •Power crisis requires structural overhaul – Iledare By Ediri Ejoh Nigeria’s electricity crisis is unlikely to be resolved in 2026, as the Federal Government has shifted the settlement of its N3.3 trillion debt to power generation companies to 2027, while major interventions in metering and transmission infrastructure are also expected to extend beyond this year. The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, disclosed this during an interview with Arise News yesterday, adding that the government had paid N1.23 trillion of the debt, negotiated down from an initial N6 trillion, and was exploring options to clear the outstanding balance. These include offsetting obligations against royalties and corporate income tax, as well as engaging the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, NNPC, to reduce gas costs for power generation companies. “We’re on track to finish paying the rest next year. Because we are looking at different ways to settle it,” Tegbe said. On the proposed debt offsets, he said: “You can’t take money with one hand and give it with the other hand. So, let’s net it off.” Tegbe attributed 80 per cent of the sector’s challenges to human and institutional factors, with technical issues accounting for the remaining 20 per cent. “I said the problem in power sector is 20 per cent technical, 80 per cent human,” he said, identifying poor teamwork, lack of coordination among operators, liquidity constraints and governance issues as major obstacles to efficiency. He also criticised past investment decisions, saying some projects were driven by political considerations rather than proper planning. “From a technical point of view, I will tell you the biggest issue: it is that we’ve been throwing money at wrong things,” he said. The minister said his ministry was reviewing ongoing projects to prioritise investments capable of improving electricity access. Tegbe recently projected that stable electricity supply could take another three to five years. He also announced plans for a $2 billion East-West Super Grid project to expand transmission capacity from about 4,000MW to 19,000MW. The proposed network would link Funtua, Gwagwalada, Ikot Ekpene, Benin, Epe and Ilorin. Procurement is under way, with completion expected within two years, according to the minister. Reacting, Professor Emeritus of Petroleum Economics, Wumi Iledare, called for a structural overhaul, warning that replacing individuals would not resolve the sector’s deep-rooted problems. “Darkness arising from persistent electricity failures in Nigeria is not fundamentally a consequence of individual ineptitude; it is a manifestation of institutional failure,” he said. Iledare argued that decentralisation could encourage competition, investment and subnational participation, but stressed that it must be backed by effective regulation, institutional capacity and accountability. “Ultimately, Nigeria needs institutional reform, not m

item.title: Eruption Extends Iwo Jima’s Beach
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Eruption Extends Iwo Jima’s… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search October 26 November 11 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison October 26 November 11 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison October 26 November 11 Curtain Toggle 2-Up A volcanic eruption in the shallows near Iwo Jima has extended the Japanese island’s famed black sand beaches, at least temporarily. Signs of unrest began in late October 2026. On October 27, seismic sensors recorded a sharp uptick in activity, and Japan’s Meteorological Agency reported that the first photographs of the eruption were captured. Soon after, sensors on several satellites began to capture an array of observations. The OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 captured the left image on October 26, when the coast was still quiet. On November 11, Landsat 9 got its first clear view of the land the submarine volcano has built (right). A shortwave-infrared signature, a sign of the eruption’s heat, is shown in orange. A faint gray volcanic plume drifts southeast of the vent, and a streak of floating pumice stretches across the water in the same direction. A false-color backscatter radar image from the NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) satellite offered an even earlier look at the eruption. On October 28, despite heavy cloud cover, the radar detected a large disturbance in the water in the same area that erupted in December 2023. When the clouds cleared in early November, the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) and VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) sensors on NASA and NOAA satellites also captured signs of the ongoing eruption’s volcanic plumes and infrared signature . Japan’s Coast Guard released a report on November 16 confirming the formation of new land connected to the pre-existing beach. The eruption appears to have added roughly 50 hectares (125 acres) of new beach, about the area of 90 American football fields. That would enlarge the island by about 1.7 percent. The new land adjoins the southeast beach where American troops landed on February 19, 1945, beginning one of the bloodiest battles in the history of the U.S. Marines. The location of the eruption is no surprise to scientists. In addition to the 2023 eruption off the southeast coast, Iwo Jima had an eruption off its west coast in August 2025, said Daniel Slayback, a scientist at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center. How long the new land will persist remains an open question. New land created by the 2023 eruption succumbed to wave action after

item.title: Delta attack: Nobody will kill at rallies if law catches up with them — Falana
item.description: Senior Advocate of Nigeria and human rights activist Femi Falana has warned that recurring pre-election violence and political killings will persist unless perpetrators face swift prosecution and legal accountability ahead of the 2027 polls. Speaking on Channels Television ’s Politics Today on Monday, Falana described recent election-related fatalities — including killings reported in Delta State — as tragic and preventable, blaming entrenched impunity across past tragedies and political clashes. He noted that attacks on political figures and convoys are often met with little or no consequence, creating a climate where violent tactics are normalized. “The stakes are high for the political class, but in this unfortunate incident, nothing may come of it. Yesterday, we lost scores of people in Bayelsa State in what was a boat accident. What would happen? Donations have already started; who is the owner of the boat? “Nobody would have thought they were going to kill people in a rally if they know that the law will catch up with them,” Falana said. Falana urged the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), civil society, and other stakeholders to step up rather than leaving political affairs solely to politicians. “Arrests may be made in Delta State, but I am challenging the Nigerian Bar Association and the human rights community to intervene very decisively because if we leave the affairs of our country in the hands of politicians, we will run into a serious crisis,” he said. He further called on the NBA to mobilize lawyers to help the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) prosecute electoral offenders, arguing that INEC is already stretched by pre-election and post-election litigation and lacks the bandwidth to handle prosecutions alone. Beyond electoral violence and credibility concerns — such as voter register cleanup, official accountability, and result transmission — Falana pressed political parties and candidates to campaign on concrete governance issues rather than ethnicity or religion. He pointed to unspent basic education funds at the state level, compulsory health insurance and child rights laws, fuel subsidy controversies, crude-for-loans commitments, and stalled refinery rehabilitations as areas requiring public debate and enforcement. Despite mounting frustrations, Falana rejected the idea that Nigeria is beyond hope, arguing that existing laws can drive change if citizens, the media, and civil society enforce accountability. “So for me it’s not a hopeless situation. It is about promoting debates and that’s what I miss,” he said, adding that Nigerians must discuss issues and hold leaders accountable rather than merely watching political spectacles The post Delta attack: Nobody will kill at rallies if law catches up with them — Falana appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Intrigues, factors shaping battle for 7 North-West states
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo, Haruna Aliyu, Musa Ubandawaki, Idris Salisu, Fauziyya Lawal, Hadiza Yusuf & Muhammad Inuwa THE battle for the seven North-West state government houses of Kaduna, Jigawa, Sokoto, Kano, Kebbi, Katsina and Zamfara is gathering momentum ahead of the February 6, 2027 governorship elections, with incumbent governors seeking fresh mandates amid growing opposition activities, political defections and shifting alliances. Although the All Progressives Congress, APC, controls all the states and enjoys the advantage of incumbency, the emerging political landscape suggests that none of the contests can be taken for granted. The African Democratic Congress, ADC, is positioning itself as a rallying platform for politicians dissatisfied with the ruling party, while the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, is banking on its traditional grassroots structures and political networks. In Kaduna, Governor Uba Sani faces a familiar challenger, Isa Ashiru of the ADC. In Jigawa, Governor Umar Namadi confronts Mustapha Sule Lamido of the PDP and Senator Sabo Muhammad Nakudu of the ADC. Sokoto presents a potentially bruising contest between Governor Ahmed Aliyu and former Deputy Governor Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, while Kano Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf faces opposition candidates and the political consequences of his separation from former political benefactor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso. In Kebbi, Governor Nasir Idris faces former Attorney-General of the Federation, Abubakar Malami, who is seeking to capitalise on public dissatisfaction. Katsina Governor Dikko Umaru Radda is challenged by Senators Yakubu Lado Danmarke and Ahmad Babba Kaita of the PDP and ADC respectively. In Zamfara, Governor Dauda Lawal, who defected from the PDP to the APC, faces Senator Kabiru Marafa of the National Democratic Congress, NDC, and other opposition candidates. Across the seven states, insecurity, particularly banditry, kidnapping, attacks on rural communities and displacement, is emerging as a defining electoral issue. Economic hardship, unemployment, poverty and the rising cost of living will also influence voters’ assessment of the incumbents. The governors must contend with internal party rivalries and the challenge of translating government projects and political appointments into votes. The opposition, on its part, must convert public dissatisfaction, endorsements and growing political visibility into effective grassroots mobilisation. item.title: Cisco and OpenAI pitch eBPF kernel plugins as the way to tame the patchpocalypse
item.description: Cisco and OpenAI have released an open-source tool called Shirudo to implement compensating controls in Linux, potentially improving security for users who can’t quickly patch newly discovered software flaws. Shirudo relies on eBPF, the technology that makes it possible to run sandboxed programs in the Linux kernel. eBPF programs are effectively kernel plug-ins but don’t get unrestricted access to system resources. Developers have mostly used eBPF to create network functions that enable things like the open source Kubernetes observability and security tool Cilium , a Cloud Native Computing Foundation project. Cisco and OpenAI think eBPF can help organizations cope with the flood of 100,000-plus software flaws reported this year, many after the debut of AI-powered bug finders. The increased volume of flaws, and patches to fix them, is a problem for many organizations which already struggle to test fixes or find change windows in which to implement them. That problem has seen greater interest in “compensating controls” – changes to applications or infrastructure that harden them against flaws or malware, without requiring a patch. With Shirudo, Cisco and OpenAI are suggesting two things: The privileges eBPF programs enjoy make them a fine way to implement compensating controls for Linux; Agents should scan your infrastructure for vulnerabilities, then use tools like OpenAI’s Codex to write compensating controls as eBPF programs at machine speed. “Shirudo” is apparently the Japanese word for “shield,” so Cisco and OpenAI have called the eBPF programs the tool creates “shields.” The two companies envision humans checking every shield Shirudo creates before putting it into production. Shirudo is open source and available here . The two companies say they’ve already demonstrated it could mitigate the recently discovered flaws in Java without requiring downtime for an Elasticsearch implementation. Cisco and OpenAI are not alone in advocating for compensating controls. Third-party software maintenance outfits like Rimini Street have used them for years to protect software when their clients no longer have the right to access patches. VMware has introduced “virtual patching.” Palo Alto Networks and Rapid 7 also like this approach, and offer automation to develop controls. Where Cisco and OpenAI differ is their decision to make Shirudo open source , and their ambition that other players adapt and advance it. That offer is not entirely altruistic, as if Shirudo takes off it could create more demand for Codex. Cisco’s angle comes from the fact it owns Isovalent, an early champion of eBPF and the creator of both Cilium and the Tetragon sub-project on which Shirudo is based. Switchzilla is using eBPF in other products, so normalizing its use through an open source project can’t hurt. ®

item.title: Anthropic says Claude solved an age-old math problem, but the written proof is 250,000 pages of slop
item.description: The leaders of the great model houses, Anthropic's Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Sam Altman, desperately want the world to believe AI is the skeleton key which will unlock the secrets of the universe. But if the AI can’t explain what it’s “proven,” are we actually any closer to understanding anything, or have we simply built another black box? That question is top of mind among mathematicians and computer scientists this week after Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge claimed to have solved a mathematical conjecture so elusive it's gone unproven for more than 150 years. The fact that this note came out one day after Anthropic's record-setting IPO is a coincidence, we're sure. In a four-page post to his website, the researcher described how with the help of Claude, he believes he has proven the Riemann Hypothesis, one of seven Millennium problems so complex and so important that the Clay Mathematics Institute has offered a $1 million prize to anyone who is successful in solving them. The Riemann Hypothesis, conjectured by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, contends that all nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function – those with a real part between zero and one – have a real part equal to 1/2. Confused? Don’t worry. We’ve linked to an explainer that goes into more detail here . What's important is that, if the Riemann Hypothesis is right, mathematicians can place tighter bounds on the difference between the actual distribution of prime numbers and mathematical estimates of that distribution. Researchers have previously attempted to disprove the conjecture through computational brute force, and therein have shown the hypothesis holds to at least 10 trillion zeros . There’s reason to believe that the Riemann Hypothesis is accurate, but the possibility remains that over a sufficiently long series the pattern might diverge. And so, more than 150 years after Riemann published his hypothesis, it has remained just that. Alpöge’s proof, if it can even be called that, is now the subject of great debate. The four pages in which Alpöge remarks on the discoveries he and Claude made aren’t exactly a proof, but rather 14 tarballs worth of Lean code totaling roughly 240 MB. Lean is an open source programming language commonly used to help validate mathematical proofs. The Clay Mathematics Institute, which oversees the seven Millennium Problems, has promoted the Riemann Hypothesis from “unsolved” to “active” status, but it is not yet considered solved. For Clay to consider the problem solved and award the prize, the proposed solution must be published in a qualifying outlet, remain available for scrutiny for at least two years, and receive broad acceptance from the mathematics community. As it stands, Alpöge describes the 250,000 pages of text generated by the model for its written proof as a “massive unreadable travesty of ‘slop.’” Not long after Alpöge's remarks and Lean code were published, Stanford mathematician Ravi Vakil released a nearly 1,000-pag

item.title: Will astronauts farm on the moon? Scientists successfully grow potatoes in simulated lunar dust
item.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

It's no secret that NASA is working towards a permanent presence on the moon. The space agency even plans to build a moon base for its astronauts to call home. But humans living inside lunar habitats around the clock will need three square meals a day, so researchers have been working on how to grow food on the moon. To that end, a team from the College of Agricultural Sciences at Oregon State University have been raising potatoes in simulated moon dust with promising results. The researchers published their findings Nov. 20 in the Microgravity science journal. "We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter," Aymeric Goyer, associate professor at OSU's Department of Botany and Plant Pathology, said in a statement . "That's an important step toward developing reliable food production systems that could support long-term human exploration of the moon." To grow the spuds, the scientists used five different materials that are similar to regolith , the dust and rocks that cover the moon's surface. The moon contains various regions with unique surface makeups, so the materials they used simulated regolith from both lunar mare and lunar highland regions. The secret ingredient was vermicompost, a soil that's rich in nutrients. The team added different levels of vermicompost to the simulated regolith to grow the potatoes. They figured out that fake regolith mixed with 30 percent vermicompost worked about as well as growing potatoes with regular soil. Oregon State University researchers David Handy and Aymeric Goyer studying potatoes grown in lunar regolith. (Image credit: Aymeric Goyer/David Handy/OSU) "We believe the compost helps balance some of the toxicity we see in lunar regolith by reducing plant exposure to harmful compounds," David Handy, a postdoctoral researcher in Goyer's lab, said in the same statement. The idea is that astronauts in the future could bring a little nutrient-rich soil with them and mix it with regolith to grow potatoes. After all, it'd cost a ton to ship all that food from Earth. NASA funding supported this research.

item.title: Trump halts Iowa detonation, says new governor to blame if it blows accidentally
item.description: President Trump took to social media Monday afternoon to announce that he has ordered the US military to halt plans to detonate 68 deteriorating barrels of lead azide at an Army ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa. Trump claimed that the fate of the unstable, highly explosive material is now in the hands of a federal court and Rob Sand, Iowa's governor-elect, who won't be sworn into office until January. The Army had planned to detonate the barrels on November 20, but delayed the blast on Thursday amid public outcry and a legal challenge from environmental groups. The explosion will launch a plume of toxic gases and neurotoxic lead that could reach up to 100 miles away from the Iowa facility, the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP). Iowa residents and officials said they learned of the detonation only days beforehand. The environmental groups, led by Earthjustice, claimed in an emergency court filing that the Army had not fully considered safer options for disposing of the lead azide before planning the detonation. item.title: Inception - possibly a ShinyHunters reboot - claims seven victims in a week
item.description: Don't mind the recent arrests. The ShinyHunters extortion gang may still be operating, just under the new name of Inception, according to Okta's threat intelligence group. ShinyHunters is the brash cybercriminal group that, most recently, breached rival gang Clop before hacking the FBI , resulting in at least three arrests of key suspects in September and October. The crims - and their old data leak site - have since gone dark. “While this threat cluster has changed their brand affiliation, the operators remain active in targeting organizations with voice phishing attacks and account takeovers resulting in data theft and extortion,” Okta threat hunters Moussa Diallo and Katie Nickels said on Monday. Okta tracks this threat cluster as O-UNC-053 - the “O-UNC” prefix stands for an Okta Uncategorized cluster, and it uses this label before formally attributing the activity to a named threat group. While Okta hasn't formally confirmed O-UNC-053 to be the same crime crew as ShinyHunters, the identity and access management provider’s researchers note that it does use nearly identical social engineering tactics: voice phishing , during which the scammers trick targets into entering credentials into phishing pages and approving multi-factor authentication (MFA). Plus, they note: O-UNC-053 operators change the themes of their phishing domains about every four to six weeks, and they also post claimed victims on ShinyHunters’ data leak site. In November, however, organizations targeted by O-UNC-053 began appearing on a new data leak site branded as Inception and not ShinyHunters. The first five - Advanced Micro Devices, Cigna Healthcare, Paychex, PepsiCo, and Henry Schein - appeared November 17 on the site, and all were marked “leaked.” Soon after, security maven Dominic Alvieri questioned if Inception was linked to ShinyHunters. “ShinyHunters are not all in jail,” he wrote on social media. On November 19, AutoZone appeared on the site, with Inception again claiming to have leaked the auto-parts retailer's files. On Saturday, EV technology firm Lucid Group joined the claimed victims. None of the seven companies have confirmed breaches, and none responded to The Register ’s inquiries. We will update this story when we receive more information. Okta Threat Intelligence “is unable to validate if published data is authentic,” the researchers said in response to our questions. In the Monday report, the Okta team does note that Inception’s new data leak site listings “included multiple targets for which Okta Threat Intelligence previously observed O-UNC-053 infrastructure registration.” The infrastructure was registered between six and 19 days before Inception listed the companies on its leak site, and this gap “is consistent with prior shifts from Com-affiliated actors,” Diallo and Nickels added. item.title: The Apple Watch Series 12 is cheaper than ever ahead of Black Friday
item.description: The Apple Watch Series 12 is on sale in multiple configurations. | Photo: Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge If you’re still sporting an Apple Watch that launched five or so years ago, now is a good time to upgrade. Apple’s latest smartwatch, the 42mm Apple Watch Series 12 with Wi-Fi and GPS connectivity, has dropped to a new all-time low of $299 ($100 off) at Amazon and Walmart , beating its most sale price by $30. If you prefer a larger size, the 46mm model is on sale for $349 ($100 off) at Amazon and Walmart , beating its previous low by $30. Apple Watch Series 12 Where to Buy: $399 $299 at Amazon (GPS, 42mm) $399 $299 at Walmart (GPS, 42mm) $449 $349 at Amazon (GPS, 46mm) The Series 12 stands out compared to previous models with its new AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, which are made possible by Apple’s new S11 chip. For example, the watch can alert you when it detects sounds like a doorbell, alarm, or even a baby’s cry, while other upcoming features like Live Rewind and Siri Recap lets you look back at a transcript of the previous 15 seconds of conversation and get a high-level overview of the conversations you had that day. The new chip also makes Siri more responsive, so you can get answers to questions with less waiting around. It’s not all about AI, though. The Series 12 also features redesigned health sensors that can now track your heart rate every five seconds even when you’re not exercising, which is particularly help if you have a chronic condition and need to keep a closer eye on your heart rate. It also introduces a new readiness score to help you decide how prepared your body is for the day. Other highlights include easier navigation with simple pinch gestures, and faster charging, which helps to make up for the fact that battery life is rated at up to 24 hours on a single charge, just like the previous-generation model. In our testing, the watch went from 20 to 64 percent charge in just 20 minutes, making it relatively easy to top up while showering or getting ready for the day. Tariq is the Editor-in-Chief of Space.com based out of our New York City office and joined the team in 2001, first as an intern and staff writer, and later as an editor. He covers human spaceflight, exploration and space science, as well as skywatching and entertainment. He became Space.com's Managing Editor in 2009 and Editor-in-Chief in 2019. In October 2022, Tariq received the Harry Kolcum Award for excellence in space reporting from the National Space Club Florida Committee. In June 2025, the National Space Society awarded him the Space Pioneer Award for Excellence in Mass Media at the International Space Development Conference in Orlando, Florida.

Hailing from Stockton, California (where he attended the same high school as NASA astronaut Jose Hernandez), Tariq studied print journalism and astronomy at the University of Southern California in Los Angeles, earning a bachelor's degree in journalism in 1999 along with a minor in astronomy. He then served as a staff reporter for The Los Angeles Times covering education and city beats in La Habra and Fullerton in Orange County for the Our Times sections.

In 2000, Tariq became the city reporter for the Huntington Beach Independent, a weekly publication of the Los Angeles Times, covering local politics and events, crime, business and environmental issues. He left the Los Angeles Times in 2001 to study science journalism at New York University, where he earned a master's degree in 2002 from NYU's Science and Environmental Reporting Program (now the Science, Health and Environmental Reporting Program) under the direction of space reporter William Burrows.

Tariq first joined Space.com as an intern in September 2001 while also serving as a research assistant for nutrition writer Gary Taubes and writing freelance projects, where his work appeared in The Scientist and Laboratory Equipment Magazine. He became a full-time reporter covering spaceflight in 2004, with this first launch being NASA's STS-114 Return to Flight mission in July 2005.

Tariq is also an Eagle Scout (yes, he has the Space Exploration merit badge) and went to Space Camp four times as a kid and a fifth time as an adult. When not writing about space, you can find Tariq watching the latest Star Trek TV series, sci-fi movies and reading about hippos, his favorite animal. You can find Tariq at Space.com and as the co-host to the This Week In Space podcast with space historian Rod Pyle on the TWiT network. To see his latest project, you can follow Tariq on Twitter @tariqjmalik.

item.title: Amazon scoops up AI accelerator tech to keep chips busy at all times
item.description: Amazon has agreed to buy AI optimization technology from an Israeli startup in a bid to speed up its inference operations. The house of Bezos on Monday announced a deal to purchase proprietary AI acceleration tech from Decart AI, known as the Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), for an undisclosed amount. Amazon also plans to bring Decart’s three founders and their engineering team into the fold. Decart’s DOS is designed to push AI hardware closer to its maximum performance across different AI models and hardware platforms. The company claims that most AI chips live their lives without reaching their full potential – practically a sin in this age of increased hardware costs and limited availability – and DOS aims to fix that by operating between the model and the chip, optimizing kernels, compilers, and runtimes for the underlying hardware “so every core stays busy.” DOS is hardware-agnostic, with Decart saying it supports Nvidia GPUs, Google TPUs, and, most critically for our purposes here, AWS Trainium chips. “More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost,” Peter DeSantis, Amazon SVP of foundational AI models, custom silicon, and quantum computing, said in the announcement. “That's the pillar Trainium and our AI efforts are built on, and from our earliest work with Decart, we knew they … would help us push it even further.” Decart doesn’t offer much in the way of details about its proprietary AI-maxxing tech, but claims it can reduce latency, improve throughput, and reduce the costs associated with training and inference runs. An Amazon spokesperson clarified to The Register that the deal is an asset purchase and not a full company acquisition, with Amazon only acquiring DOS and the tech behind it as well as personnel. As for what may become of Decart after the deal, that’s unclear. Amazon told us to reach out to Decart to learn what may happen to any remaining employees and the company’s other technology, but we didn’t hear back. Along with offering its optimization stack, Decart has a couple of different AI models: Lucy, a live video model marketed toward advertisers, live streamers, and the like; and Oasis, a world model AI marketed toward companies working on embodied AI applications. Decart’s non-DOS assets weren’t mentioned in the press release, and per the Amazon spokesperson we talked to, that means they weren’t part of the deal. We can’t imagine that the Decart team is too upset about the potential abandonment of those models, though: While neither company has disclosed a price, Bloomberg claims its sources value the deal at around $7.5 billion. If Bloomberg's figure is accurate, that would make this deal one of the most expensive in Amazon’s history, right between its $3.9 billion acquisition of One Medical and its $8.5 billion purchase of film studio MGM . ®

item.title: NASA Awards Contract for NOAA’s Near Earth Orbit Network Program
item.description: Credit: NASA NASA, on behalf of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), has awarded a contract to Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation for the Sounder for Microwave-Based Applications (SMBA) instruments on NOAA’s Near Earth Orbit Network (NEON) satellites. The cost-plus-fixed-fee, firm-fixed-price, and time-and-materials hybrid contract has a value of $290.6 million. The period of performance runs from Nov. 23 through April 1, 2042. The work will take place at the awardee’s facility. Under the contract, Northrop Grumman will provide the design, development, production, testing, and mission support for three SMBA instruments, the next generation of low Earth orbit microwave sounders. NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, is managing the acquisition, and NOAA will own and operate the instruments and deliver the data to users worldwide. Microwave sounders provide critical measurements of temperature and moisture in the atmosphere, which significantly influence weather patterns. The SMBA instruments could improve the medium-range forecasts for NOAA’s National Weather Service. The NEON mission is a collaboration between NASA and NOAA. The mission is led by NOAA, which provides funding, technical requirements, and postlaunch operations. NASA will manage the development of the NEON satellites and launch them for NOAA. NASA and NOAA will work with commercial partners to design and build the NEON spacecraft and instruments. For information about NASA and agency programs, visit: https://www.nasa.gov -end- Liz Vlock Headquarters, Washington 202-358-1600 elizabeth.a.vlock@nasa.gov Peter Jacobs Goddard Space Flight Center, Greenbelt, Md. 301-286-3308 peter.jacobs@nasa.gov Share Details Last Updated Nov 23, 2026 Editor Jessica Taveau Location NASA Headquarters Related Terms Science Mission Directorate Goddard Space Flight Center NOAA (National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration)

item.title: Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC Strive (Nasdaq: ASST) bought no bitcoin last week and sold no stock to fund new purchases, leaving its holdings unchanged at 43,404 BTC, according to a Monday 8-K filing. The Dallas-based company reported that its bitcoin count was unchanged between Nov. 13 and Nov. 20. It sold no Class A common shares, no SATA preferred shares and no SATS preferred shares in its at-the-market programs from the Nov. 13 close through the Nov. 20 close. Strive pauses after two small buys The pause follows a slowdown from the October sprint that built the stack. Strive bought 251 bitcoin for $17.5 million the prior week at an average of $69,853 per coin, after adding just 29 coins the week before that. Bitcoin traded near $61,000 on Coinbase on Monday afternoon. That is about 12.6% below the $69,853 average Strive paid for its most recent purchase. At that price, the 43,404-coin stack is worth roughly $2.65 billion. The filing gives no reason for the pause, and the company has not said whether it plans to resume weekly buying. Strive has typically disclosed its holdings on Mondays, so next week’s update will show whether the stack grows again. Most of the stack was built quickly. Strive held 28,000 bitcoin on Sept. 30 and acquired 15,124 more between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30, including a single 6,182-coin purchase. The company closed a registered offering of 7 million SATS shares on Oct. 20 for about $609 million in net proceeds, which funded much of that run. Cash and preferred holdings Strive’s cash and cash equivalents slipped to $462.4 million as of Nov. 20 from $465.3 million a week earlier, a decline of $2.9 million. The filing does not break out what drove the change. The company also still holds 505,000 shares of Strategy’s variable-rate STRC preferred stock. The fair value of that position fell to $47.3 million from $50.5 million, a drop of about $3.2 million, with the share count unchanged. Share counts were also flat. Strive reported 118,133,002 Class A shares and 9,198,107 Class B shares, for 127,331,109 effective common shares. Outstanding preferred stood at 14,030,176 shares of SATA and 7,141,037 shares of SATS, the 15% perpetual preferred it has used to fund most of its purchases. Strive’s holdings rose from 43,153 bitcoin on Nov. 6 to 43,404 on Nov. 13, and the filing shows no change since. With no common or preferred stock sold, the company raised no new capital through its offering programs last week, which left cash as its main resource for dividends and operations. Shares rally, then fade with the market Strive shares were trading near $15.55 at 3:56 p.m. ET on Monday, up about 7.1% from Friday’s close of $14.51, according to Yahoo Finance. The stock opened near $17.64, a gain of more than 20%, and gave back much of it through the session. item.title: 2027: ‘As You Do For Me, I Do For You,’ Tinubu Seeks Igbo Support In Lagos
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has appealed to Igbo residents in Lagos State to support his re-election bid in the 2027 general elections. President Tinubu made the call while addressing Igbo stakeholders at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, Iganmu, Lagos, on Monday. ﻿ President Tinubu said that though he was displeased when he lost the 2023 election in the state, which is considered a stronghold of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), the matter had been settled. “Some of you didn’t vote for me in 2023; I vex o . We don settle. Get your PVC,” he urged the crowd. Tinubu also asked if they would vote for him, to which they replied with a resounding “Yes.” After receiving assurance from the stakeholders to back his re-election bid, the president said, “Come January 16, get your PVC; you come vote. Agreement na agreement o, na Bola Tinubu be APC o. As you do for me, I do for you.” ‘Follow Who Know Road’ President Tinubu called for national unity and collective responsibility, urging Nigerians to see themselves as one people with a shared future, in the interest of the country. “You must follow who know road. I have to work hard to make sure the economy improves, to ensure that your children are in school, to eliminate crises in the universities, to build good roads that will maintain our cars. “The future is in our hands. For every one of us, our children must be in school. Because we are poor doesn’t mean they shouldn’t attend the universities,” he added. Tinubu further said the country must rise above its divisions, noting that its development depended on the participation and commitment of all its people. Also speaking, the Governor of Lagos State, Mr Babajide Sanwo-Olu, urged Igbo residents to support Tinubu’s re-election and vote for all candidates of the APC in the 2027 general elections. The governor also implored them to work for the emergence of the Deputy Governor and APC governorship candidate, Obafemi Hamzat, as the next Governor of Lagos State. During the meeting, the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi; the Minister of State for Budget and Planning, Doris Uzoka-Anite; and the former Minister of Labour and Employment, Nkiruka Onyejeocha, as well as other Igbo leaders and stakeholders, assured President Tinubu of their support. The Independent National Electoral Commission said Peter Obi, who was the candidate of the Labour Party, polled 582,454 votes in Lagos, higher than the 572,606 votes polled by Tinubu in the February 25, 2023 presidential election. Lagos, Nigeria’s commercial hub, has one of the highest numbers of registered voters for the 2027 general elections. Emphasising the electoral importance of Lagos, Tinubu described it as a big deal to him. ”To me, Lagos is the big deal. How can you have seven million registered voters and produce 100,000-200,000 votes? That’s failure. “Even if you win, and say, ‘A win is a win,’ no. item.title: Bitcoin Price Fades Near $61,000 as Stocks Soar on Huang’s Return
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Fades Near $61,000 as Stocks Soar on Huang’s Return The bitcoin price slipped back to near $61,100 on Monday afternoon, giving up nearly all of its morning spike even as Wall Street held one of its biggest rallies in years on Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. Bitcoin jumped above $64,000 shortly after the Nvidia news broke before 10 a.m. ET and topped out near $64,500. The move reversed within hours , and the bitcoin price dipped to around $60,800 by 2:45 p.m. ET. It remains up only modestly on the day. The round trip was costly for leveraged traders. Bitcoin liquidations reached about $321 million , with short bets making up $224 million of that total. Liquidations across the broader crypto market topped $762 million. Stocks hold gains as bitcoin fades Stocks kept climbing while bitcoin slid. The Nasdaq Composite was up about 6.9% near 24,170 at about 3:40 p.m. ET, while the S&P 500 gained about 5% and the Dow rose about 3.2%. The S&P 500 had fallen seven straight days before Monday. Nvidia (NVDA) led the move, trading near $165.66, up about 32% from Friday’s close of $125.53. The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, CEO and director, 12 days after he resigned. A stronger dollar may be weighing on the bitcoin price. The dollar index rose about 0.65% to 104.40 , its strongest level since April 2025, as the stock rebound put more Federal Reserve rate hikes back in play. The Fed meets Dec. 8-9, and a quarter-point hike remains the base case. Adam Haeems, head of asset management at Tesseract Group, pointed to steady selling during U.S. market hours since Huang first stepped down. “Bitcoin has fallen in seven of the eight U.S. sessions since Huang went, today’s included, and last week each session’s fall lined up with that day’s ETF outflow,” he said. Crypto stocks keep most of their gains Crypto stocks held up far better than the bitcoin price. Strategy (MSTR) was up about 9.3% near $85.03 in afternoon trading, after it disclosed a purchase of 457 bitcoin last week. Coinbase (COIN) gained about 6.7% to near $108.78, Robinhood (HOOD) rose about 8.8% to near $67.64 and Circle (CRCL) added about 8% to near $51.33. Miners with AI data center businesses posted the biggest moves. IREN (IREN) jumped about 23% to near $14.57, CleanSpark (CLSK) rose about 12.6% and MARA Holdings (MARA) gained about 10%. Core Scientific (CORZ) climbed about 9.4% and Riot Platforms (RIOT) added about 7.1%. ETF flows and inflation data are next Monday’s spot bitcoin ETF flows are the next test. The funds lost about $1.79 billion last week, their fourth straight week of net outflows, as bitcoin slid toward $58,000 on Friday and hit a weekend low near $55,100. “Tonight’s ETF flow figure is the first real test of this bounce,” Haeems said. Strong inflows would suggest buyers are returning, while another round of outflows would raise doubts about how far the rebound can run. Traders also face Wednesday’s inflati

item.description: It was the most simple of questions. On Monday afternoon, during a NASA news conference about the International Space Station, Space News reporter Jeff Foust asked about an upcoming launch of a Russian spacecraft. "It's my understanding there's another cargo mission going to the ISS this week, a Russian Progress," Foust said. "Can you confirm that, and give the date and time that will launch?" This Progress MS-36 cargo launch, mind you, is presently scheduled for fewer than 16 hours from now, at 10:13 UTC (05:13 am ET) on Tuesday. item.title: Surveillance pricing uses our personal data to make us pay more
item.description: “It costs what it costs” is a mindset I’ve found useful when encountering a sizable, but highly necessary or desired, expense. The sentiment encourages me to accept the price because that’s the accepted value of the gadget, app, or service that I really need or want. But with surveillance pricing, that comfort is no longer a given. I could end up paying more for my TV because of where I am or more for a software subscription because of my age. Surveillance pricing leverages data collected from our web history , smart devices , and apps with the goal of getting us to pay more. That obfuscates the value of products, challenges smart shopping and budgets, and makes it harder for people to get products and services at a fair price. Read full article Comments

item.title: 2027: Armed Men Who Killed Four NDC Campaign Members Said I Was Their Target, Omo-Agege
item.description: Former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege has alleged that the gunmen who attacked his campaign team in Delta State, killing four people, repeatedly shouted his name and declared their intention to kill him. Omo-Agege, who is seeking election to the Delta Central Senatorial District on the platform of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 general elections, said he escaped the attack through the intervention of his Department of State Services (DSS) escorts. He spoke on Monday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today . ﻿ Recounting the incident, the former deputy senate president said he heard the attackers repeatedly shouting that they wanted to kill him while opening fire at the campaign venue. “Right there at the venue, while they were shooting, we could hear them say, ‘It is Omo-Agege we want to kill. We must kill Omo-Agege.’ “But I was lucky because my DSS details were very professional. In fact, after God, the only reason I am alive today is because of the DSS operatives who were with me,” he said. Omo-Agege described the incident as a premeditated attack, alleging that there had been a build-up to the violence. He questioned why he would be singled out for elimination when several other politicians were also contesting elective positions. The former lawmaker said the attackers struck less than five minutes after he began addressing supporters at the campaign venue. According to him, he had moved towards the side of his vehicle to make eye contact with members of the audience when the gunshots rang out. “It was by divine intervention. As I was speaking, I just moved over to the side of the vehicle to be able to make eye contact with those I was speaking with. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started,” he said. The former deputy senate president said four members of his campaign organisation were killed, while about 15 others sustained injuries, with some in critical condition. ﻿ In a statement issued earlier on Monday by his media adviser, Sunny Areh, Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation said he survived an assassination attempt during a campaign tour in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. Areh alleged that armed men opened fire on the senator and his entourage while he was addressing supporters during a campaign visit. The organisation called for an independent and thorough investigation by the Nigeria Police Force, while appealing to the Inspector-General of Police, the DSS, INEC, civil society organisations and the international community to ensure the safety of political candidates and their supporters. It also urged supporters to remain calm and avoid retaliation, adding that its ward-to-ward campaign activities across Delta Central would continue. item.title: Amazon fights Delivery Protection Act by putting stickers on its packages
item.description: Amazon is placing a sticker on some of its delivery boxes to urge customers to oppose a New York City bill. This weekend, some Amazon shoppers reported getting a delivery from Amazon with a sticker on it that reads: “NYC Council could add up to $5 per order. Act now to protect low prices.” The sticker reportedly includes a QR code that leads to a link for contacting NYC Councilmembers. The sticker encourages the package’s recipient to “Scan to tell your council member: no increases for New Yorkers.” Amazon is looking to stoke opposition to Introduction 0518-2026 ( 518 ), also known as the Delivery Protection Act. The proposed law would require Amazon and other companies with last-mile delivery facilities in the city, such as FedEx, to directly employ third-party contractors Amazon uses for making deliveries.
